records.title: RGIT Scholarship for Continuing Students
records.description: The RGIT scholarship program enables students with outstanding academic outcomes to pursue further studies. RGIT offers a range of courses that equip students with skills that enable them to make a meaningful contribution to society. Scholarships are available to students who intend to study a VET course at RGIT. The Scholarship Committee will manage the selection and allocation of funds.
records.eligibility: Selection is based on evidence that in the previous term the applicant has: submitted all assessments by set deadlines; received competency on the first attempt in all units scheduled; maintained 90 per cent or higher attendance throughout the term; and participated in a positive and diligent manner in all aspects of the course. Applicants must prepare a one-page report in support of their application which addresses the following points: why they believe they should be awarded a scholarship; why their chosen course is the best choice for them; and any other information they wish to include that supports the application.

records.title: Griffith University International Postgraduate Research Scholarship
records.description: Griffith University awards Griffith University International Postgraduate Research Scholarships (GUIPRS) via a competitive application process to candidates commencing or enrolled in a Higher Degree Research (HDR) program. The fee offset provided through the award of a GUIPRS will remove the liability of the HDR candidate to pay program tuition fees for the tenure of the award. This website sets out the allowances and conditions attached to the GUIPRS award. A limited number of GUIPRS may be allocated to achieve specific strategic objectives. In such cases, there may be additional eligibility requirements or variations to the procedure for selection and award. The GUIPRS Conditions of Award will be amended to reflect the variations applicable to the awardee.
records.eligibility: Not be a domestic student, as defined as being a student who is an Australian citizen or; an Australian permanent resident or holder of an Australian Permanent Humanitarian visa or; a New Zealand citizen.; be commencing or enrolled in a HDR program (for which GUIPRS support is available) at Griffith University.
records.deadline: For information on when to apply through the Continuous Scholarship Round and intake dates please see Key dates (https://www.griffith.edu.au/research-study/scholarships#keydates).

records.title: Eric Dubsky Memorial Engineering Leadership Scholarship
records.description: Eric Dubsky was an electrical engineer who immigrated to Australia from Nazi occupied Austria shortly before the outbreak of World War II in 1939. Initially with his father and then as chairman and managing director he developed a small manufacturer Vulcan Electrics Pty Ltd into one of the top 100 companies in Australia - Vulcan Industries Australia Ltd. Vulcan produced a range of innovative domestic and commercial products and had 2000 employees. He employed engineering students as trainees with the company, many of whom became leaders with Vulcan and other engineering companies. This award continues his legacy by providing young engineers with the opportunity to develop into future leaders of Australian industry.
records.eligibility: Applicants must: Be An Australian citizen; A New Zealand citizen; Australian permanent resident; Australian humanitarian visa holder; An International student; Enrolled in any single or double undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Engineering at a Monash campus in Australia.; Have completed a minimum of 48 credit points in their Engineering degree.

records.eligibility: To be considered for this fellowship, you must:; be completing a degree in the Faculty of Business and Economics (Bachelor, Honours, Master or PhD) in 2026 specialising in Economics or have previously completed a degree from FBE specialising in Economics (Bachelor, Honours, Master or PhD); be undertaking or intending to undertake postgraduate studies in Economics at an overseas university or research institution in 2027.; be no more than 27 years of age at the time of the award
records.amount_comment: Each fellowship is paid in two equal instalments: the first upon acceptance of the scholarship and evidence of full-time enrolment at the overseas university or research institution, and the second upon evidence of continued full-time enrolment at the overseas university or research institution.

records.title: Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship
records.description: The Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship is offered to high-achieving students who are enrolling in a bachelor degree and are citizens of countries where international educational opportunities are limited by financial disadvantage.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must: Be a citizen of a country with a Gross Domestic Product per capita of US$10,000 or less based on data published by the World Bank. For the complete list of countries, see: Eligible countries. Have applied for and meet the entry requirements for an Overseas Fee place in a bachelor degree. Have completed secondary school outside Australia or a foundation program in Australia. Not have previously undertaken tertiary studies (excluding extension studies completed as part of a year 12 program).
records.amount_comment: This scholarship provides a 25 per cent fee sponsorship for the duration of the course.

records.title: Scientia Scholarship
records.description: The UNSW Scientia Scholarship has been established to encourage students who achieve a raw ATAR* score (or equivalent) of 99.90 or above in an Australian Senior Secondary Certificate, or equivalent qualification, to undertake full-time undergraduate study at UNSW.
records.eligibility: To be eligible, applicants must meet all the following criteria: Be commencing an eligible UNSW undergraduate degree program. The scholarship is available to students in most undergraduate degree programs, except for the BMed MD program. Only a very limited number of scholarships may be available to students enrolling in the BMed MD program. Must have achieved a raw ATAR score (or equivalent) of 99.90 or above (not including adjustment factors) in an Australian Senior Secondary Certificate in the year prior to commencement of study at UNSW. International applicants undertaking this qualification must be residing in Australia and attending an Australian High School to be considered. Australian Citizens undertaking an assessable international senior secondary qualification with an equivalent ATAR of 99.90 or above are also considered. Students who have completed the International Baccalaureate (IB) must achieve a score of 45 to be considered eligible. Must have submitted a UAC Undergraduate Admission application and listed UNSW as one of their preferences by the December Round 2 offer round (18 December 2024).
records.amount_comment: The scholarships are valued at $10,000 per year for the minimum duration of the degree.

records.title: Destination Australia Scholarship
records.description: Destination Australia is an Australian Government initiative, offering amounts of up to $15,000 (AUD) per year to eligible students who wish to study full time and live in regional Australia. Our Destination Australia scholarship program is open to international & domestic students who wish to study Animation, Games, Film, Audio & Music on-campus at SAE Byron Bay in 2024.
records.eligibility: Applicants are to be domestic or onshore international students wishing to commence study in a Bachelor Program in 2024. NOTE: International students must be residing in Australia with a valid VISA.; Applicants must be a commencing student enrolled full time at the SAE Byron Bay (on-campus study); Scholarships will be prioritized to applicants from underrepresented groups such as low socio−economic status, those who are first in family to tertiary study, those living with a disability and First Nations people.; Must demonstrate and maintain residency in the Northern Rivers Region at the time of commencing study for the duration of the scholarship Northern.; Applicants must meet SAEs published domestic or international entry requirements.

records.title: Avondale Student Research Scholarship
records.description: These scholarships provide opportunity for students to participate in a program of supervised research. Students can extend their knowledge, develop their analytical and critical thinking, and their communication skills. The scholarship is open to all Avondale students who are enrolled beyond the first year of their course and have a GPA of 5.0 or above.
records.eligibility: The scholarship holder (scholar) is required to complete 160 hours of research. This may take place in a block of full-time work, or may be negotiated with the project supervisor to take place part-time over a longer period. Research may be conducted on campus (Lake Macquarie or Sydney) or off campus. At the completion of the project, the scholar and their supervisor will give an oral presentation of their research. The supervisor will be responsible for organising a suitable format, time and venue for the presentation in consultation with the scholar.

records.eligibility: Please contact University of Tasmania for further information.

records.title: Sydney Global Mobility Joint PhD Travel Scholarship

records.amount_comment: This scholarship will provide a one-off payment of $AUD 5000 for one year.

records.amount_comment: Full fee remission.

records.title: ANU College of Law International Partners Scholarship
records.description: Each year the ANU College of Law may offer a number of awards known as the ANU College of Law International Partners Scholarship with the aim of attracting and supporting top quality international postgraduate students to the ANU College of Law.
records.eligibility: is an International student; has applied for admission to the Master of Laws (LLM) program at the ANU College of Law; has achieved a minimum GPA of 5.0 out of 7.0 (or equivalent) in their relevant undergraduate degree; has graduated from a law program or will have graduated by the time of taking up the scholarship from one of the following Universities:; Peking University - Beijing, China; University of Tokyo - Japan; has been shortlisted by one of the above Universities.
records.amount_comment: 100% fee waiver of tuition for one year

records.title: Doherty PhD Supplementary Scholarship
records.description: Each year the John Curtin School of Medical Research in the ANU College of Health and Medicine may offer an award known as the Doherty PhD Supplementary Scholarship with the aim to attract students of high calibre, with clinical qualifications, to pursue postgraduate studies at the JCSMR involving a clinical research project, in order to facilitate interaction between basic biomedical science and clinical research. The award was established in honour of Professor Peter Doherty, who shared the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine with Professor Rolf Zinkernagel in 1996, for work done at JCSMR.
records.eligibility: is awarded and continues to hold an Australian Government Research Training Program (AGRTP) Stipend Scholarship, or a similar living expenses PhD scholarship; is enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy at the John Curtin School of Medical Research; holds an Australian Bachelor Honours degree with First Class Honours or equivalent,and has research publications and/or relevant research experience.

records.title: Doherty Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is offered by the John Curtin School of Medical Research (JCSMR). The Doherty Scholarship (Clinical) is to attract students of high calibre with clinical qualifications to pursue graduate research involving a clinical research project for a PhD degree at the JCSMR.
records.eligibility: Students of high calibre with clinical qualifications. Preference given to Australian or New Zealand Citizens and Permanent Residents of Australia however International students will also be considered.

records.title: Emergency Accommodation Bursary
records.description: The Emergency Accommodation Bursary is designed to assist students who are currently enrolled at the ANU as an award-status student, and are experiencing unexpected financial difficulty in meeting their accommodation costs. Assistance is not ongoing and the bursary is not designed for pre-arrival costs or as a method of income. Funds are granted subject to eligibility. Applications are assessed and awarded at the discretion of the Bursary Review Committee. The Committee will determine the amount of any bursary granted from an assessment of the students need and the availability of funds. The Emergency Accommodation Bursary can provide up to 52 weeks of financial support over the course of your current level of study at the ANU. If living on campus, bursary funds will be paid directly to a student's residential account.
records.eligibility: is a domestic or international student; is enrolled in an undergraduate, honours or postgraduate degree offered by the University; is enrolled in at least one course (if a coursework student) or at least 24 units (if a higher degree research student) during the period; has not received the Award for 52 weeks during their current level of study; if residing in an on-campus residence, does not have any serious breaches of their Occupancy Agreement recorded; can demonstrate a change in personal circumstances that has affected their ability to meet financial obligations; can demonstrate financial hardship.
records.amount_comment: Scholarship Value : Variable

records.title: Olin J Eggen Research Award
records.description: The Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics (RSAA) offers the Olin J Eggen Research Award to up to 3 outstanding international students commencing in the PhD program at RSAA. Funding for this Award is made possible by an endowment setup to commemorate the contributions of the late Professor Olin J Eggen. Professor Eggen, a native of Wisconsin, USA, was Director of Mt Stromlo Observatory from 1966 through 1977, a period that saw considerable growth and with it the foundation of the high international regard in which the Observatory (now the Research School of Astronomy & Astrophysics) is held. The objective of the Award is to support outstanding international students to enable them to pursue a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program in Astronomy & Astrophysics based in the Research School of Astronomy & Astrophysics.
records.eligibility: is enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Astronomy & Astrophysics based in the Research School of Astronomy & Astrophysics; and is and remains an international student; has a demonstrated track record of significant research that contributes to the field of Astronomy & Astrophysics.

records.title: Replacing Animals in Medical Research Honours Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is to assist students enrolled in a one year Honours program, undertaking research utilising non-animal alternative methods to replace the use of animals or animal products in medical research.
records.eligibility: is a domestic or international student; receives an offer of admission to an honours specialisation in the ANU College of Science or the ANU College of Health and Medicine; is undertaking research utilising non-animal alternative methods to replace the use of animals or animal products in medical research.

records.title: Research School of Accounting Pre-Master Training Program Scholarship
records.description: Each year the Research School of Accounting within the ANU College of Business and Economics may offer a number of awards known as the Research School of Accounting Pre-Master Training Program Scholarship (the Award). The objective of the Award is to continue the long-standing partnership and successful pre-masters agreement between ANU and selected Partners. Funding for this Award has been provided by the Research School of Accounting.
records.eligibility: is an international student; is completing, or has completed a recognised Pre-Master Training Program at a home institution; is enrolled in, or has received an offer of admission to the Master of Accounting (4 semesters), or the Master of Professional Accounting (3 semesters).

records.title: Research Training Program (RTP) International Fee Offset Scholarship
records.description: Each year the Commonwealth Department of Education and Training provides funding to Universities to award scholarships to International students undertaking Higher Degree Research programs under the Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP). Note the duration of this scholarship has been updated from 3 years to 3.5 years following the VCs announcement relating to scholarship changes in effect from 1.10.2022. Candidates now no longer have to apply to extend this scholarship from 3 years to 3.5 years.
records.eligibility: The Commonwealth Scholarship Guidelines (Research) 2017 set the basis for the conditions of award and outline the basic eligibility requirements for this scholarship.; The ANU has established an RTP Policy & Procedure which outlines the standards, processes and conditions for this scholarship. These documents are available from the reference document section of this page.; Candidates are ranked and scholarships are awarded based on a competitive ranking process, to the top ranked candidates, subject to evidence they meet merit-based selection criteria, and subject to confirmation of a qualified supervisor, space and resources being available, in an area of research that is aligned with ANU research strategy.
records.amount_comment: Full Tuition fees for 3.5 years

records.title: Ross Taylor PhD Supplementary Scholarship in Geochemistry
records.description: Each year the Research School of Earth Sciences may offer an award known as the Ross Taylor PhD Supplementary Scholarship in Geochemistry. Funding for this Award has been provided by generous donations from associates of Ross Taylor, and matching School funds. Professor Taylor has made an outstanding contribution in geochemistry and as a pioneer of lunar science. His work spans the moon, the Earths continental crust, island arc rocks and beyond. Fifty years ago, the Canberra scientist Professor Ross Taylor made one of the big discoveries about the nature of the moon. Professor Taylor was chosen by NASA as the best person to analyze the first moon rocks brought back by Apollo 11. The launchpad for Taylors success was the environment of excellence at ANU, which included an almost identical lab to NASA. Taylors involvement with the moon was not his only contribution to science. Apart from many academic awards, he was elected as a Foreign Associate of the US National Academy of Sciences in 1994 and he was appointed a Companion of the Order of Australia in 2008.
records.eligibility: a domestic or international student; enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Earth Sciences at the ANU.

records.title: Stan and Jessie Holland Scholarship
records.description: Each year the ANU College of Science (the College) may offer up to two awards (one for a PhD candidate and one for an MPhil candidate) known as the Stan & Jessie Holland Scholarship (the Award). Funding for this Award has been endowed to the ANU in memory of his parents Stan and Jessie Holland by their eldest son. The objective of the Award is to support outstanding Aboriginal, African or Pasifika candidates to enable them to pursue a Higher Degree by Research (HDR) program in the field of ecology and environmental science, based in the College of Science.
records.eligibility: is enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy or Master of Philosophy in ecology or environmental science, based in the College of Science; has successfully obtained an offer of admission to an ANU HDR program; identifies as Aboriginal, African or Pasifika descent.

records.title: Taiyang and Loong PhD Supplementary Scholarship
records.description: Each year the John Curtin School of Medical Research (JCSMR), ANU College of Health and Medicine may offer up to six awards known as the Taiyang and Loong PhD Supplementary Scholarship (the Award). The objective/s of the Award are to encourage interest in computational biology, accelerate knowledge and skill development and cultivate an entrepreneurial research and learning environment for PhD students.
records.eligibility: A domestic and/or international student; Have obtained first-class Honours, or equivalent in the field of computer science or a related discipline; Enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy at the ANU in the subject area of computational biology, with the John Curtin School of Medical Research; A recipient of an ANU approved HDR base stipend scholarship; Candidates must demonstrate keen interest in developing new computer science tools and applications that directly address real-world biomedical problems. PhD projects will focus on specific biological questions, with defined potential industry partners and computational areas.

records.title: Australia Awards Scholarships
records.description: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards administered by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade that aim to contribute to the development needs of Australia's partner countries in line with bilateral and regional agreements. The Scholarships provide opportunities for people from developing countries, particularly those countries located in the Indo-Pacific region, to undertake full time undergraduate or postgraduate study at participating Australian institutions. Since 1997, James Cook University has provided quality academic and personal support to over many hundreds of Australia Awards Scholarship students from more than 40 countries. Australia Awards Scholarships are offered for the minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training and generally cover tuition fees, air travel, and allowances to cover accommodation expenses, text books, study materials and basic living expenses.

records.title: 2026 Stanford Advanced Materials College Scholarship
records.description: As a trusted supplier of advanced materials for industries such as aerospace, technology, healthcare, and energy, Stanford Advanced Materials (SAM) has long been focused on the industrial applications and development trends of rare metals. To explore the potential of rare metals fully, we invite outstanding students to join us in discussing their applications and future directions. We are also proud to announce the establishment of the 2025 College Scholarship by Stanford Advanced Materials to support students who demonstrate excellence in this field.
records.eligibility: Open to high school, undergraduate, and graduate students worldwide. records.title: High Precision Rotation Sensor
records.description: Ground rotation sensors have wide applications, such as precision instrumentation, environment monitoring, and rotational seismology, as well as for improving the sensitivities of gravitation wave detectors. Currently available rotation sensors have issues of either low sensitivities or too fragile/too large to be used in the field. At UWA we are developing a compact, and robust with a high sensitivity rotation sensor using many innovative technologies. This PhD project is to build, characterize and field test the rotation sensor.
records.eligibility: Honours or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or Experimental Physics.; Meet the UWA PhD entrance requirements with adequate English.; Have a high academic achievement in the coursework.; Demonstrated research capabilities through high quality research thesis and/or published peer-reviewed journal papers.
records.amount_comment: Stipend scholarship / Tuition fee scholarship

records.title: Adelaide Merit Scholarship (15%)
records.description: The Adelaide Merit Scholarship provides a 15% tuition fee reduction for international students starting an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree and is automatically awarded at the time of offer to applicants who have achieved a credit average and shown strong academic commitment. This scholarship supports international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees who are committed to their academic achievement.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; be an international student; be applying to study a CRICOS registered bachelor degree (minimum 72 units / 1.5 years equivalent) after the application of any credit/RPL, or a CRICOS registered master degree (minimum 48 units / 1 year equivalent) after the application of any credit/RPL, at Adelaide University; satisfy one of the following in the qualification used as the basis of admission to the Adelaide University degree:; Undergraduate only:; A minimum ATAR of 75 for students who have completed the Australian Senior Secondary Certificate of Education (SSCE) (or international equivalent for any other secondary certificate).; Successful completion of a competency-based vocational qualification in Australia with an overall non-graded pass.; Undergraduate and postgraduate:; A minimum overall Grade Point Average (GPA) of 4.5 (on a 7.0 scale) for an award completed at Adelaide University (or with a comparable score for a qualification completed at an Australian University).; A minimum overall Grade Point Average (GPA) of 5.0 (on a 7.0 scale) or comparable.; A minimum overall Grade Point Average (GPA) of 4.5 (on a 7.0 scale) or equivalent from a program completed at an approved Adelaide University pathway provider.; not be applying to study one of the Excluded Programs; not be an Australia Awards recipient; not be an International Sponsored Student entitled to a tuition fee waiver equal to or greater than the scholarship

records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; be an international student; be applying to study a CRICOS registered bachelor degree (minimum 72 units / 1.5 years equivalent) after the application of any credit / RPL, or a CRICOS registered master degree (minimum 48 units / 1 year equivalent) after the application of any credit / RPL, at Adelaide University; provide verifiable evidence that they have previously completed a degree at Adelaide University or the University of South Australia or the University of Adelaide and / or have completed at least one semester of a Study Abroad Program at one of these institutions; not be applying to study one of the Excluded Programs; not be an Australia Awards recipient; not be an International Sponsored Student entitled to a tuition fee waiver equal to or greater than the scholarship value, in which case the fee waiver amount will apply.

records.title: 2027 - Knight Hennessy Scholars Program at Stanford University
records.description: The Knight-Hennessy Scholars Program supports outstanding graduate students from around the world to pursue an eligible graduate degree at Stanford University in the United States. The program offers scholars the opportunity to join a diverse, multidisciplinary community while participating in leadership development alongside their Stanford studies.
records.eligibility: To be eligible to apply, applicants must:; have earned, in January 2020 or later, a U.S. bachelor's degree or an equivalent qualification from a recognised college or university; apply to, be accepted by and enrol in an eligible full-time Stanford graduate degree program; meet one of the following conditions:; apply separately but concurrently to Knight-Hennessy Scholars and a full-time Stanford graduate degree program, commencing both in the same year; be a current Stanford graduate student applying to add a new full-time Stanford graduate degree program, commencing both Knight-Hennessy Scholars and the new program in the same year; be a current Stanford PhD student in the first year of enrolment, applying to begin Knight-Hennessy Scholars in the second year of PhD enrolment.
records.amount_comment: funding for up to three years of graduate study at Stanford, depending on the length of the degree program; a stipend for living and academic expenses, plus a travel stipend for one annual trip to and from Stanford; leadership development opportunities

records.title: Understand and manipulate quantum geometry in kagome metals (PhD scholarship)
records.description: This PhD project will investigate quantum geometry-driven electronic transport in kagome lattices as a pathway beyond the scaling limits of conventional silicon electronics. By engineering crystal symmetry and magnetic order through controlled chemical doping, the research aims to tune the quantum metric and realize giant nonlinear Hall effects in transition-metal kagome compounds. High-quality single crystals will be synthesised, fabricated into micro-devices, and studied via physical property measurements to probe quantum-metric responses. This project will deliver fundamental insights into quantum materials and establish a platform for low-power quantum devices.
records.eligibility: You need to meet the entry requirements for QUT's Doctor of Philosophy, including any English language requirements.; enrol as a full-time, internal student (unless approval for part-time and/or external study is obtained); commence your degree by 1 Oct 2026; have an honours or master degree in one of these areas:; physics; theoretical chemistry; materials science and engineering.
records.amount_comment: You'll receive a stipend of $40,000 per annum for a maximum duration of 3.5 years while undertaking a QUT PhD. The duration includes an extension of up to six months if approved for your candidature. This is the full-time, tax exempt rate which will index annually.; You will receive a tuition fee offset/sponsorship, covering the cost of your tuition fees for the first four full-time equivalent years of your doctoral studies.; As the scholarship recipient, you will have the opportunity to work with a team of leading researchers, to undertake your own innovative research in and across the field.; During this project, you need to work in domestic and international institutions such as Australia's Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO). While we would encourage you to apply for their institutional grants, the fund can only be used for non-stipend purpose (e.g. experimental consumables, travel grant, and open-access publication charge).

records.title: SQA Undergraduate Research Scholarship
records.description: The program aims to provide students partway through their undergraduate degree with an opportunity to develop their research skills and inspire them to consider further quantum technology research or related activities. Candidates undertake an exciting 6-week project at one of SQAâ€™s four partner universities, supervised by a leading quantum researcher. Several projects can also be completed partly or fully online. The scholarships are open to students studying at SQA partner universities or attending a university in NSW. The project period is for 6 weeks in December to March (exact dates will depend on project supervisor availability), on a full-time basis (35 hours/week for six weeks during normal working hours unless advised otherwise by the supervisor). Flexible arrangements can be made to accommodate, for example, carer responsibilities.

records.title: The Elephant in the Study: Working Latin Literature for the Enslaved PhD Scholarship
records.description: Applications are invited for a PhD scholarship in Latin literature and/or Roman slavery. The scholarship is supported by the Australian National University (ANU) and is part of an Australian Research Council (ARC) Future Fellowship. The Elephant in the Study: Working Latin Literature for the Enslaved is an ARC supported inquiry into the role and significance of enslaved co-authors in the production of Latin literature between approximately 100 BCE and 100 CE. The project will examine the implications of enslaved collaboration for the form, content and reception of classical Latin literature, and probe how such collaboration changes our notion of the histories of literature, authorship, and slavery.
records.eligibility: Continuation based on academic performance; 6 month extension available.

records.title: Browse CQUniversity Scholarships
records.description: We believe a quality education can be for everyone – regardless of background, location, or life circumstances. That’s why we offer a variety of scholarships and bursaries to cater for all student needs. This can include financial support to assist with living expenses, and non-deferrable costs such as textbooks, uniforms, technology, course-specific equipment, travel costs associated with compulsory residential schools and unpaid placement, accommodation, and general living expenses such as rent, groceries and fuel. Whether you’re a commencing student or continuing your studies, receiving a scholarship can help balance your studies and life commitments. A scholarship looks good on your resume and may open the door to industry networks and work experience opportunities.

records.title: Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness PhD Scholarship
records.description: The Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness (PMCS) welcomes applications from suitably qualified scholars for a place in the Melbourne Law School’s (MLS) PhD program for commencement in 2025. The successful candidate will be working under a supervisory team which will include PMCS academic staff, MLS academic staff affiliated with the Centre, and/or a co-supervisor from another University of Melbourne faculty if appropriate.
records.eligibility: Applicants must be eligible for acceptance by the University of Melbourne into a PhD program. This scholarship is conditional upon acceptance into the PhD program at the Melbourne Law School, and the applicants need to meet the entry requirements of the Law School PhD program which can be found here. Applicants must also: have not completed a PhD previously. Be able to commence their PhD in 2025 – with a preferred start date in February 2025.
records.amount_comment: Scholarship recipients undertaking a doctoral degree at the Peter McMullin Centre on Statelessness will be awarded: Full fee offset for up to four years. An annual stipend of AUD $38,500 (tax free) (2025 full-time study rate). The scholarship is available for a maximum period of 3.5 years pro rata. The living allowance may be indexed annually and includes limited paid sick, maternity and parenting leave. A relocation allowance of AUD $2,000 may be granted for candidates who need to move from outside Victoria or AUD $3,000 for candidates who need to move from outside Australia. Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) Single Membership for international students who require a student visa to study in Australia.

records.title: Brian Gray Scholarship
records.description: The Brian Gray Scholarship program provides up to four scholarships valued at $15,000 each to support students in finance, economics, actuarial science, econometrics, statistics or related disciplines who intend to focus full-time on their studies and research. The scholarship also provides the opportunity to devote time to an agreed research topic benefiting, where possible, from access to Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) expertise and data. Scholarship holders may also be able to gain valuable work experience with APRA during their final year of study. The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) and the Reserve Bank of Australia have established the Brian Gray Scholarship in memory of Brian Gray, who died on 24 August 2001 while serving as Executive General Manager of APRA’s Policy, Research and Consulting Division.
records.eligibility: If you are a full-time honours year or PhD student studying a topic of relevance to prudential supervision and are an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident you are eligible to apply. Postgraduate students may also apply.Eligible subject areas include: banking, insurance and superannuation (particularly the prudential supervision and financial soundness of these industries), econometrics, statistical studies.
records.amount_comment: The Brian Gray Scholarship program will fund up to four scholarships annually, to the value of $15,000 each.

records.title: Clayton Adam Florence Wilson Award for Biomechanics and Spine Research
records.description: The Clayton Adam Florence Wilson Award is available to promote spine research at QUT, and honours the stellar contribution to scientific innovation in spine research made by our former Research Director, Professor Clayton Adam. Clayton joined QUT in 1999 and dedicated his work to helping children with spinal disorders, and to improving treatment outcomes for patients who undergo spinal surgery. He brought together a dedicated team of researchers, scientists, engineers, surgeons and industry partners to perform cutting edge research aimed at minimising risks and improving spinal surgery results for patients. Clayton’s leadership of the research program resulted in QUT receiving a substantial bequest from a donor impressed by his work: the Florence Wilson Bequest. In 2015, Clayton was diagnosed with a terminal illness yet continued his active research during treatment until early 2018. Sadly, his health battle ended in March 2018, but his dedication and contribution to biomechanics and spinal research will long be remembered and admired.
records.eligibility: You must have experience in biomechanics and/or spine research. Further eligibility criteria will be provided following successful acceptance of your application.

records.title: Australian Government Research Training Program
records.description: The Commonwealth Governments Research Training Program (RTP) provides funding to universities to support the research training of both domestic and international higher degree research (HDR) candidates. The funding provided through the RTP offers the provision for universities to administer and award a number of stipend scholarships known as Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarships. These awards are governed by the Commonwealth Scholarship Guidelines (Research) 2017. Griffith University awards RTP Stipends via a competitive application process to candidates commencing or enrolled in a HDR program. RTP Stipends are provided to assist with candidates general living costs and do not cover program tuition fees. This website sets out the allowances and conditions attached to the RTP Stipend award.
records.eligibility: be commencing or enrolled in a HDR program (for which RTP support is available) at Griffith University.; not be receiving income from another source to support the candidates general living costs that provides a benefit greater than 75% of the GUPRS stipend rate to undertake the proposed program. Income unrelated to the candidates HDR program, or income received for the candidates HDR program but not for the purposes of supporting general living costs, is not to be taken into account.
records.amount_comment: RTP Stipends are provided to assist with candidates’ general living costs and do not cover program tuition fees.

records.title: Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship

records.amount_comment: Valued at 50% of tuition fees.

records.title: La Trobe Flexible Research Scholarship (Flex) - Candidates With Disabilities
records.description: In order to maximize opportunities for students with disabilities to study higher degrees by research, La Trobe University is offering the Flexible Research Scholarship to eligible applicants with disabilities, who already hold a Research Training Program (RTP) stipend or a La Trobe University Graduate Research Scholarship (LTGRS) stipend. This scholarship provides individually tailored support, providing a longer period of time for completion of a graduate research degree and payment of a stipend, extended periods of leave of absence, and provide access to additional funding for research related costs associated with having a disability.
records.eligibility: currently be receiving a Research Training Program (RTP) stipend or a La Trobe University Graduate Research Scholarship (LTGRS) stipend, or have accepted an offer of RTP or LTGRS, and have a disability that is attributable to one or more intellectual, cognitive, neurological, sensory, or physical impairments or to one or more impairments attributable to a psychiatric condition; and the impairment or impairments are, or are likely to be, permanent; and (b) the impairment or impairments result in substantially reduced functional capacity to undertake, or psychosocial functioning in undertaking, one or more of the following.
records.amount_comment: Up to 18 month extension to RTP or LTGRS stipend for doctoral candidates and up to 8 month extension for research masters candidates

records.title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarships

records.eligibility: To be eligible for an RTP Stipend a candidate must not be receiving income from another source related to their Higher Degree by Research, to support the candidates general living costs while undertaking their research degree, if that income is greater than 75% of the candidates RTP Stipend rate. Income unrelated to the candidates research degree or income received for the candidates research degree, but not for the purpose of supporting general living costs, will not be taken into account; To be eligible for an RTP Fees Offset a candidate must not be receiving an equivalent award or scholarship from the Commonwealth Government designed to offset tuition fees for their Higher Degree by Research.; In 2025 all domestic applicants will be offered an RTP Fees Offset provided they are not receiving an equivalent award or scholarship from the Commonwealth designed to offset Higher Degree by Research tuition fees.; The scholarship holder is expected to diligently pursue the degree for which they are enrolled. Continued payment of the scholarship is therefore subject to the scholarship holder making satisfactory academic progress and terminates on the expiry of the scholarship or on submission of the thesis for examination, whichever is the sooner

records.title: Predictive farming PhD Scholarship: improving risk management with AI-enhanced weather forecasts and crop models
records.description: This project will investigate artificial intelligence (AI) to improve weather forecasts and use crop models for making better farming decisions. The expected outcome is protocols for integrating AI-enhanced weather forecasts and crop models into farm management and planning tools. This is expected to result in farmers making more informed decisions that optimize resource use, boost crop yields, and enhance overall farm productivity and profitability while minimizing environmental impact.
records.eligibility: To be eligible applicants must:; Have completed an Honours Degree with First Class or 2A Honours, or equivalent level, or a master's degree with significant research component.; Not be receiving equivalent support providing a benefit greater than 75% of the student's stipend rate.; Be an Australian citizen or Permanent Resident, or a New Zealand citizen.; Meet participating university PhD admission requirements.; Meet university English language requirements.; Not have previously completed a PhD.; Be able to commence the Program in the year of the offer.; Enrol as a full-time PhD student.; Be prepared to be located at the project location(s) that the host university has approved and, if required, comply with the host university's external enrolment procedures.
records.amount_comment: Stipend of AUD $47,000 (2025 rate); A project expense and development package of up to $13,000 per annum.; Maximum period of tenure of an award is 4 years. Periods of study already undertaken towards the degree will be deducted from the period of tenure.

records.title: Using Systems Engineering to Model Neuropathic Pain (PhD Scholarship)
records.description: Neuropathic pain effects "1 in every 10 adults over the age of 30". The treatments available for neuropathic pain can at best be described as having "moderate efficacy". Due to the nature of neuropathic pain, the ability to scientifically study and understand its fundamental causes has been limited to animal models and trials. There are over 27 animal models for neuropathic pain where pain has been induced by macroscopic & microscopic nerve lesions, chemotherapy, viral infections and diabetes mellitus. Looking at clinical studies, the current research process is to propose a model, conduct animal tests and then evaluate whether the original model is consistent with results. This is difficult as it requires humans to evaluate pain in animals which cannot be directly measured. This process is not systematic in the way it comes up with models and has thus resulted in many models of limited effectiveness.
records.eligibility: You need to meet the entry requirements for a QUT research degree / Doctor of Philosophy / professional doctorate, including any English language requirements.; enrol as a full-time, internal student; have a background in either mechanical or medical engineering.

records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam; be applying offshore from Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam (RMIT Vietnam students who completed cross-campus studies and immediately apply for the same qualification (course) in Melbourne campus are not eligible); be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the course commencement; achieve Australian equivalent grade GPA of 2.5 or 70% average or ATAR 75 in your qualifying qualification at the time of application; hold a full or conditional offer letter to commence studies in Vocational Education, Associate Degree*, Bachelor’s degree*, Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma or Masters by Coursework degree; not be an existing RMIT University student (existing ELICOS or Foundation Studies may be qualified and will be notified after Foundation Studies completion).
records.amount_comment: The value of the scholarship is a 20% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the eligible course(s)* as outlined in your offer letter.

records.title: FUNED - RMIT Scholarship
records.description: If you are an international student from Mexico applying for a Masters by Coursework program at RMIT University, you may be eligible for this jointly funded scholarship by RMIT and the Mexican Foundation for Education, Technology and Science (FUNED).
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Mexico; have applied for a Masters by Coursework at RMIT; satisfy the general and specific requirements of the FUNED credit scholarship; meet the academic requirements for entry to RMIT and have been given an unconditional offer of a place in the program; have been awarded the FUNED credit scholarship; be commencing full time enrolment as an international student at RMIT in Melbourne.
records.amount_comment: RMIT UP Academic English Bursary for Latin American students if you are required to study ELICOS; tuition fee support by RMIT to the value of 25% of the tuition fees for Masters by Coursework program for a maximum of two years.

records.title: RMIT UP Academic English Bursary for Asia
records.description: If you are a citizen of Cambodia, Japan, Laos, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam this bursary provides a tuition fee discount on your Academic English course.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Cambodia, Japan, Laos, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam; applying from Australia or overseas; enrol in an Academic English course at RMIT University Pathways (RMIT UP) commencing in 2026 or 2027 for 10 weeks or more; not be the recipient of any other English Language scholarship (including external scholarships); be a commencing RMIT UP student (including extending your program in Australia).
records.amount_comment: 10% of the total program fee in 2026 study period for an Academic English course (you pay $491 per week after the discount); 20% of the total program fee in 2027 study period for an Academic English course (you pay $452 per week after the discount)

records.title: School of Art Honours Travelling Grant
records.description: For art honours students who can demonstrate outstanding academic achievement; worth up to $4,000.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this grant you must:; be enrolled full-time in Semester 1 and 2 in 2026, in either the:; Bachelor of Arts (Fine Art) (Honours) (BH052); Bachelor of Arts (Photography) (Honours) (BH125); have achieved high distinction or distinction grades during Semester 1 2026; be undertaking travel related to your art/studio practice; submit your own original art works with your application

records.title: Nepal $10,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship offers talented international students from Nepal AUD $10,000 per year towards their studies at Macquarie University. The scholarship is available for the full duration of an eligible Bachelor's and Master's coursework degree. For students enrolled in sessions, AUD $10,000 will be credited in the second session of the first year of enrolment, followed by AUD $5,000 credited in each subsequent session for the remainder of the degree. For students enrolled in tems, AUD $7,500 will be credited in the third term of the first year of enrolment, followed by AUD $2,500 credited in each subsequent term for the remainder of the degree.
records.eligibility: Be an international full fee-paying student.Be a citizen of Nepal.Be commencing full-time in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Macquarie University in 2027 and beyond (excluding Graduate Certificates, Bachelor of Clinical Science, Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours), Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Physiotherapy, Master of Clinical Audiology, Master of Clinical Psychology, Master of Clinical Neuropsychology, Master of Organisational Psychology, Master of Professional Psychology, Master of Speech and Language Pathology).Accept your Letter of Offer and pay the commencement fee by the Acceptance Deadline.Must not be a recipient of a government sponsorship or scholarship that covers full tuition fees, unless approved by Macquarie University Scholarships Team.Please note: The annual number of scholarship recipients may vary according to the availability of funding and the number of eligible candidates and will only be confirmed when an offer letter is made.

records.title: ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award
records.description: The Australian National University (ANU) ('the University') may offer a number of awards known as the ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award ('the Award'). The objective of the Award is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs offered by the University. Funding for this Award is provided by the Australian National University.
records.eligibility: The Award is available to an ANU student who:; is an international student; is a new commencing student or a continuing student who has received an offer of admission to a higher AQF level of studies; holds residential status in one of the following Countries or Regions:; China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR); Japan; Mongolia; The Democratic People's Republic of Korea
records.amount_comment: 20% off your first-year tuition fees.

records.title: American Australian Association Veterans' Fund
records.description: The American Australian Association (AAA) established its Veterans' Fund in 2017 to provide much needed financial support and assistance to Australian and American honorably discharged post-9/11 military veterans to pursue study in each other's countries respectively. With more than 40 veteran scholars and alumni and US $1.5 million awarded to date, the AAA is committed to investing in the future of veterans by supporting educational opportunities which build new skills and create prosperous post-military careers.
records.eligibility: Please Contact ANU for more information about Eligibility.

records.title: Centre of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century Research Grant
records.description: Each year, the Research School of Earth Sciences (RSES) within the College of Science and Medicine and Fenner School of Environment and Society (FSES) within the College of Systems and Society may offer a number of awards known as the Centre of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century Research Grant. The objective of the Award is to encourage students to undertake a research project in climate, weather, or related fields. Funding for this Award has been provided by ARC Centre of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century.
records.eligibility: The Award is available each year to a commencing or continuing ANU student who:; is a domestic student or international student; receives an offer of admission to an Honours program offered by RSES/FSES; has a career GPA of 6 or higher.

records.title: Joyce Fildes Honours Scholarship in Medical Science
records.description: Each year, the John Curtin School of Medical Research (JCSMR) within the ANU College of Science and Medicine may offer a number of awards known as the Joyce Fildes Honours Scholarship in Medical Science. The objective of the Award is to support students undertaking their Honours project, with research conducted in any area of medical science. Funding for this Award has been provided in memory of its donor, Dr Joyce Fildes, a former staff member of the John Curtin School of Medical Research.
records.eligibility: The scholarship is available to an applicant:; who is an International or domestic student; who is enrolled in an Honours year at the John Curtin School of Medical Research; whose Honours project is in any field of biomedical research conducted at the John Curtin School of Medical Research.

records.title: Leonard and Margaret Doman Undergraduate Scholarship for Flute
records.description: This scholarship is offered by the ANU College of Arts and Social Sciences.
records.eligibility: Selection is made on the basis of applicants meeting the eligibility criteria. Other factors, such as interview at time of audition, may be taken into consideration.

records.title: Stephen & Helen Wurm PhD Scholarship in Asia-Pacific Linguistics
records.description: Each year the School of Culture History and Language (CHL), in the ANU College of Asia and the Pacific (CAP), may offer an award known as the Stephen and Helen Wurm PhD Scholarship in Asia-Pacific Linguistics. This Award provides funding for an outstanding domestic or international student, to enable them to pursue a PhD program in Linguistics, based in the CHL, and study a lesser-described Asia-Pacific language, or languages.
records.eligibility: Continuation based on academic performance; 6 month extension available.

records.title: Taiwan Australian National University Scholarship
records.description: In 2023, ANU re-signed an agreement with the Department of International and Cross-Strait Education of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (hereunder referred to as "DICE") to continue the Taiwan Australian National University Scholarship until 2028. The scholarship program commenced in 2013 and provides tuition fees and stipends for up to 5 Taiwanese students per year to undertake PhD studies at ANU over the course of the five year agreement. The scholarships will be jointly funded by ANU and DICE.
records.eligibility: Continuation based on academic performance; 6 month extension available.

records.title: 2027 Paid Placement Support Guarantee
records.description: This scholarship supports international students who have mandatory placement units but are not doing Co-op courses. Students receive $10,000 (undergraduate) or $5,000 (postgraduate) in instalments to support them while completing their placement.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship, students must: be a commencing international student, be enrolled in an eligible coursework course that requires mandatory placements, enrol in mandatory placement units, be eligible to study in Australia with a valid visa, and meet the additional terms and conditions set out on the scholarship webpage.

records.title: 2027 Global Achiever Scholarship
records.description: This tuition fee scholarship provides eligible international students 15% off annual tuition fees for the duration of their course. This scholarship cannot be combined with other tuition fee scholarships.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must: be an international student (not a study abroad, exchange or online student), be enrolling as a commencing student in 2027, be enrolling in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Federation University Australia, be eligible to study in Australia with a valid visa, meet the additional terms and conditions as set out below, and not be in receipt of any other merit-based and/or tuition fee scholarships.

records.title: Archdiocese of Brisbane Theology Scholarship
records.description: Established in 1997 by the Archdiocese of Brisbane to provide support and encouragement for postgraduate study in theology.
records.eligibility: Enrolment in Semester 1, 2027; Faculty: Theology and Philosophy; Course: any ACU postgraduate Theology and Philosophy degree; Campus: Brisbane; Residence within the Archdiocese of Brisbane.
records.amount_comment: The scholarship is valued at $4,000, to be paid in one lump sum

records.title: Excellence Scholarship
records.description: Excellence Scholarships are awarded to those who demonstrate high academic achievement, as well as leadership skills and community involvement. As an Excellence Scholar, you will be awarded with 50% tuition remission for any single or approved combined undergraduate degree (excluding the Bond Medical Program and Diploma entry students), and will commence at Bond in either the January, May or September semester.
records.eligibility: To be eligible to apply for this scholarship, you must:; Be one of the following:; an Australian or New Zealand citizen, or an Australian permanent resident currently completing or completed* Year 12 (or equivalent) inside or outside of Australia ; an Australian permanent resident completing or completed high school outside Australia; an international student completing or completed* Year 12 (or equivalent) in Australia and; Achieve a minimum of ATAR 92.00 or IB Diploma 34; Hold a demonstrated record of leadership, initiative and service to your school and/or community.; Meet the standard entry requirements for your chosen program of study.
records.amount_comment: Provides 50% tuition remission for any single or approved combined undergraduate degree (excluding the Bond Medical Program and Diploma entry students).

records.title: Live, Earn and Learn Scholarship
records.description: The Live, Earn and Learn Scholarship is designed specifically for international students who have received an offer to study at our Rockhampton North campus. Through this scholarship, you can excel academically while building practical experience in Central Queensland. You'll receive a 35% accommodation scholarship at Capricornia College (terms and conditions apply), work part-time on campus or in the local community, and immerse yourself in a vibrant campus lifestyle. Availability for 2027 intakes is currently under review. Updates will be published on this page and communicated to eligible future students when available.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following requirements:; Have applied and received an offer to study at the Rockhampton North campus in an eligible term.; Have applied to live at our on-campus student residence during your study.
records.amount_comment: 35% of accommodation cost and paid part-time work.

records.title: 2026 - Semester 2 - Curtin On-Campus Accommodation Equity Bursary - Bentley
records.description: The Curtin On-Campus Accommodation Equity Bursary (the Scholarship) has been established to provide assistance for domestic and international students living in on-campus accommodation at Curtin Bentley who are experiencing financial hardship.
records.eligibility: Applicants must meet all of the following criteria to be eligible to apply for the Scholarship:; Domestic or international student; Have applied for a place (or currently residing) in one of the following on-campus accommodation residences at Curtin Bentley in a Semester 2, 2026 agreement at the time of application:; St. Catherine's College ,Twin Dolphin Hall, Kurrajong Village, Erica Underwood House, Guild House, Vickery House; Have a minimum Course Weighted Average (CWA) of 50 (if applicable) at the time of applying

records.title: Determining actual crop water use for maximising the Water Circular Economy (WCE) in irrigated cotton production systems
records.description: Supporting a PhD candidate advancing sustainable irrigation and water management in irrigated cotton systems.
records.eligibility: To be eligible you must:; meet Deakin's PhD entry requirements; enrol full time; hold an honours degree (first class) or an equivalent standard masters degree with a substantial research component
records.amount_comment: a stipend of $37,450 per annum tax exempt (2026 rate); a top-up of $10,000 per annum tax exempt; a relocation allowance of $500-1,500 (for single to family) for students moving from interstate

records.title: Purification of silk proteins for next generation protein-based materials
records.description: Supporting a PhD candidate to develop a new method to purify silk proteins using liquid chromatography.
records.eligibility: To be eligible you must:; meet Deakin's PhD entry requirements; enrol full time; hold an honour's degree (first class) or an equivalent standard master's degree with a substantial research component

records.title: 2026 ECU Sri Lanka Undergraduate Deans Scholarship for Academic Achievement
records.description: The ECU Sri Lanka Undergraduate Deans Scholarship for Academic Achievement is offered to students who commence studies at the ECU Sri Lanka campus and select ECU undergraduate courses in 2026. This scholarship is awarded to students who have achieved at least an 85% WAM in their first teaching period of their degree. Applicants must be enrolled full-time, have completed four units during their first teaching period, and be commencing their second teaching period in the year 2026. The scheme offers a 10% reduction in tuition fees for ECU units undertaken for the duration of their course of study at ECU's campus in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; Be a domestic(Sri Lankan citizen) or International full-time student studying at ECU's campus in Colombo, Sri Lanka.; Not be in receipt of a government scholarship or industry sponsorship.; Meet ECU's "high achievement" criteria, including maintain full time continuous study load and maintaining a WAM of 85% or above; Meet ECU's academic and English language entry requirements for the select course and any other applicable admission requirements imposed by ECU's statutes, by-laws, rules and policies and procedures.
records.amount_comment: This scholarship is awarded to students who have achieved at least an 85% WAM in their first teaching period of their degree.

records.title: 2026 ECU Creative Excellence Scholarship
records.description: The ECU Creative Excellence Scholarship is offered to international students commencing in eligible creative discipline courses at ECU. The scholarship offers a 10 percent reduction in your tuition fees for the duration of your course. The scholarship is open to future international students seeking to enrol at Edith Cowan University in one of the designated undergraduate courses.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; be an international student (not an Australian Citizen, Australian Permanent Resident, or New Zealand Citizen); study onshore at ECU City Campus; not be in receipt of a government scholarship or industry sponsorship; not be in receipt of another ECU scholarship; meet both ECU's Academic and English Proficiency entry requirements for the course and commence study onshore at ECU, Western Australia in Semester One, 2026 or Semester Two 2026; be entering into one of the eligible courses

records.title: Greg Benjamin WAAPA Music Excellence Scholarship
records.description: The Greg Benjamin WAPPA Music Excellence Scholarship is awarded to an exceptional Piano student in the jazz or classical discipline. Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Music course in Piano (jazz or classical) will automatically be considered for the Scholarship. The Scholarship is valued at $11,000.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; be an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, International Student Visa Holder or International Non-Student Visa Holder; be enrolled in W76 - Bachelor of Music - Piano (Jazz or Classical) at WAAPA; have and maintain an academic progression status of GREEN; be studying full-time on campus (60 credit points or course equivalent); not be in receipt of another scholarship over $5000 per annum; not be a previous recipient of the Greg Benjamin Entrance Scholarship.

records.title: Lincoln McCashney Memorial Scholarship
records.description: The Lincoln McCashney Memorial Scholarship is awarded to recognise an Education student who demonstrates the qualities that made the late Lincoln McCashney such an outstanding teacher, educator and mentor to many ECU students, thereby encouraging the development of those qualities and honouring Lincoln's contribution to education in WA. The scholarship is valued at up to $5,000 as a one-off payment.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship you must:; be an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, New Zealand citizen or International student; have an academic progression status of GREEN; be enrolled in a Bachelor of Education and be on track to complete a minimum of 360 credit points by end of Semester 2, 2026; be studying a minimum of 30 credit points; have a minimum weighted average mark (WAM) of 60%

records.title: 2026 Federation Merit Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded in instalments with the first instalment awarded to successful recipients at the time of offer. Ongoing scholarship instalments will be allocated to awardee's student fee account prior to the following census date and on confirmation of meeting ongoing GPA requirements.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must:; be an international student (not a study abroad, exchange or online student); be enrolling as a commencing student in 2026; be eligible to study in Australia with a valid visa; meet the additional terms and conditions as set out below.
records.amount_comment: The scholarship covers 20% of the tuition fees and is initially awarded for a period of two semesters.

records.title: 2026 Partner Scholarship
records.description: The Partner Scholarship is designed to support international students who transfer from Federation partner offshore locations to Australia to complete their studies or begin a new degree. Recipients will get a 20% tuition fee discount.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must:; be an international student transferring from a Federation offshore delivery partner or an international student who has completed XCore units with Employability.; be eligible to study in Australia with a valid visa; have completed (or be in the process of completing) an approved Federation University course or a non-award short course that is formally recognised for credit towards a Federation University degree at an approved Federation University offshore partner institution; be enrolling onshore at a Federation University Australian campus to complete the same course or commence a new eligible Federation University course.
records.amount_comment: This scholarship is awarded in instalments, with the first instalment awarded to successful recipients at the time of offer. Ongoing scholarship instalments will be allocated to awardee’s student fee account prior to census date each semester.

records.title: LATAM English Excellence Scholarship English for Academic Purposes (EAP)
records.eligibility: Available to new students only commencing in 2026 and 2027.; Available only to full fee-paying international students from Latin America; There is no separate scholarship application process for the English for Academic Purposes Scholarships. Applications for English for Academic Purposes will automatically be assessed for scholarship eligibility and eligible applicants will be notified within their Letter of Offer to the course. Eligible applicants simply need to return the course Acceptance Form and the LATAM English Excellence Scholarship Acceptance Form for the scholarship to be awarded.
records.amount_comment: 30% reduction in tuition fees.; Scholarship value is the percentage reduction specified above.

records.title: HDR Travel Grant
records.description: This grant is available to assist HDR candidates with travel costs (up to $1500) associated with research-related activities that will enhance their thesis.
records.eligibility: To be eligible to apply for this grant, you must: be currently enrolled in an HDR course; have successfully completed your Confirmation of Candidature milestone; not have submitted for examination; submit evidence of acceptance of your peer-reviewed conference submission, if you are applying to travel to a conference.

records.title: Asia & Greater China Health Merit Scholarship
records.description: If you are from Asia or Greater China and are planning to combine an English language course with one of our Health degrees, you have the opportunity to apply for this regional scholarship. It will cover 20 per cent of your total course tuition.
records.eligibility: Regional scholarships are provided based on new international students’ passports. Undergraduate students need to display a credit average from high school, and postgraduate students need to display a credit average in a previous degree.; Undergraduate and postgraduate international students must maintain a full-time study load, 1 EFTSL over a 12-month study period, to maintain their scholarship. The scholarship is applicable on tuition fee only and on first attempt subjects. Full price charged on retake subjects if previously failed. The scholarship may not be eligible for any course changes during the duration of study.

records.title: International Joint Cooperation Program Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship recognises and rewards fidelity of our Joint Cooperation Program students applying for further study at Charles Sturt University. The award provides a 25% tuition fee reduction throughout the entire duration of the program.
records.eligibility: Applicant must be a Joint Cooperation Program graduate from: Jilin University of Finance and Economics, Tianjin University of Commerce, Yangzhou University, or Yunnan University of Finance and Economics.
records.amount_comment: Value: 25% fee discount for duration of course

records.title: Collarts International Scholarship
records.description: Scholarships are now available for international students and valid for all international study applications from March 2024! Start your dream course in the creative field while we ease the financial load across your studies-eligible students can receive up to $11,000 AUD for a Bachelor or up to $3,600AUD for a Diploma.
records.eligibility: Applicants must submit a 300 word statement along with their application explaining why they should be awarded the scholarship; Approved applicants must comply with their visa conditions and obligations as Collarts students; Applicants must meet Collarts entry requirements; Scholarships are limited and awarded at the discretion of the Collarts International Team; Valid for applications received in 2024; Students must pay their fees on time to maintain eligibility; Students must maintain a credit (65%) average or above in their Collarts studies to maintain eligibility.
providers: Collarts - Australian College of the Arts

records.title: RSSS Director’s Award for Higher Degree Research
records.description: The award is a top-up to the Australian Government Research Training Program (AGRTP) Stipend Scholarship (previously the Australian Postgraduate Award), for the top-ranked Higher Degree Research applicant enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in the Research School of Social Sciences.
records.eligibility: a domestic or international student; enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in the Research School of Social Sciences at the Australian National University; has been awarded an AGRTP Stipend Scholarship.
records.amount_comment: The amount will not exceed 75% of the AGRTP, so the amount will vary based on the value of the AGRTP.

records.title: Schwarzman Scholarship
records.description: Schwarzman Scholars is an unparalleled graduate program for the next generation of young leaders, anchored in a fully-funded 10-month Masters Degree in Global Affairs at Beijings Tsinghua University. The experience encompasses unique opportunities in and outside the classroom, including extensive leadership training, a network of senior mentors, opportunities to engage in high-level interactions with Chinese leaders and visiting speakers, optional internships, career development, and travel seminars around China. Scholars will learn from world-class faculty and guest speakers about the Chinas importance on the global stage through a rigorous and dynamic core curriculum. Schwarzman Scholars prepares young leaders for a globally interconnected future and for careers in which they will join a growing alumni network of leaders who are working to build mutual understanding between China and the rest of the world. Students spend a year immersed in an international community of thinkers, innovators and senior leaders in business, politics and society. In an environment of intellectual engagement, professional development and cultural exchange, they learn from one another and pursue their academic disciplines while building their leadership capacities. This experience will expand students understanding of the world and create a growing network of global leaders that will build strong ties between China and the rest of the world.
records.eligibility: Undergraduate degree or first degree from an accredited college or university or its equivalent.; Age Requirement.; English language proficiency.
records.amount_comment: Tuition, Room & Board, Stipend & more

records.title: Stan and Jessie Holland Supplementary Scholarship
records.description: Each year the ANU College of Science (the College) may offer up to two awards (one for a PhD candidate and one for an MPhil candidate) known as the Stan & Jessie Holland Supplementary Scholarship (the Award). Funding for this Award has been endowed to the ANU in memory of his parents Stan and Jessie Holland by their eldest son. The objective of the Award is to support outstanding Aboriginal, African or Pasifika candidates to enable them to pursue a Higher Degree by Research (HDR) program in the field of ecology and environmental science, based in the College of Science.
records.eligibility: is enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy or Master of Philosophy in ecology or environmental science, based in the College of Science; is in receipt of an approved ANU HDR Base stipend scholarship; identifies as Aboriginal, African or Pasifika descent.

records.description: This award is intended to aid coursework students undertaking research in the area of Space Exploration, Moon and Mars. Funding is provided by the Boswell Technologies Endowment fund, established by Prof Roderick Boswell. The award could be used towards travel, acquiring of equipment or collaboration activities.
records.eligibility: a domestic and/or international student; enrolled full or part-time; be enrolled in a postgraduate or undergraduate program in the College of Science; undertaking a research project related to space exploration, moon and Mars.

records.description: Australia Awards are prestigious international scholarships and fellowships funded by the Australian Government. The Awards offer the next generation of global leaders an opportunity to undertake study, research and professional development.

records.title: ASEAN Partner Institution Scholarship
records.description: To recognise the strong relationship between Macquarie University and institutions in the ASEAN region, this ASEAN Partner Scholarship is awarded to prospective students from the region with a quest for knowledge. The scholarship amount is valued up to AUD $15,000 per year for talented students who are currently pursuing an undergraduate or postgraduate degree at an ASEAN partner institution.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship, you must be a full-time international student commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate (coursework) degree on-campus and meet the following criteria; Transfer from a Macquarie University ASEAN partner institution on an official dual degree or articulation program.; Achieve a minimum 65 WAM for postgraduate or a minimum 85 ATAR (or equivalent) for undergraduate applications.; Must not have received a scholarship or sponsorship from Macquarie University or another organisation for the degree; Commence study in the session and year indicated in your scholarship letter of offer.

records.title: Australia Awards Scholarships
records.description: Australia Awards Scholarship (AAS) are funded by Australian Government to provide higher education opportunities for people from developing countries to study in Australia to build the skills and knowledge to drive change as the next generation of global leaders. These scholarships aim to contribute to the development needs of Australia's partner countries in line with bilateral and regional agreements. Scholarships are mainly at postgraduate level however there is a limited number of undergraduate scholarships (country specific). Curtin will work with AAS recipients to equip you with the skills and knowledge you need to drive change and contribute to the economic and social development in your home country and build enduring connections within the community.
