We offer a diverse, inclusive and flexible working environment where our people are supported and empowered to come up with digital and data solutions with impact. You’ll work closely with your supervisors and teams on research projects that are aligned to our strategic goals. Our scholarships are awarded in partnership with Australian universities, so you’ll receive support and guidance from university supervisors alongside some of the country’s leading data and digital science experts.

records.title: ANU PhD Scholarship
records.description: This is a stipend scholarship offered by ANU Colleges to Higher Degree by Research candidates. It is normal for recipients to undertake study on a full-time basis, however, in accordance with strict criteria, the scholarship can be awarded for part-time study for Domestic candidates only. International scholars must undertake study on a full-time basis.
records.eligibility: are domestic or international students; have applied for admission to a PhD or Professional Doctorate by Research program; have a Bachelor degree with first-class honours (some Colleges may consider students with upper second-class honours), or a Master degree with a research component or equivalent from a recognized university.

records.title: Chappell and White PhD Scholarship
records.description: Once every three years the Research School of Earth Sciences may offer a PhD scholarship known as the Chappell and White PhD Scholarship (the Award). The objective of the Award is to support high achieving domestic and international PhD students who are conducting research in the areas of petrology and ore petrology. Funding for this Award has been provided by Professor Bruce Chappell and Professor Allan White. Professor Bruce Chappells career at ANU spanned more than 30 years, from 1960 to 1997. In 1967 he graduated with an ANU PhD and was awarded an ANU DSC in 1990. His sustained research contributions were recognised with many international awards including election to Fellowship of the Australian Academy of Science. Professor Allan White was a member of the Geology Department at ANU from 1960 to 1971. He was an undergraduate student of the famous Australian geologist and Antarctic explorer, Professor Sir Douglas Mawson. White left ANU to establish the Department of Geology at La Trobe University.
records.eligibility: a domestic and/or international student; enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Earth Sciences and are conducting research in the areas of petrology and ore petrology at the University; holds a Bachelor degree with first-class honours, or a Master degree with a research component or equivalent from a recognized university.

records.title: Chris Heyde & Joe Gani Scholarship
records.description: Professor Chris Heyde and Professor Joe Gani were well known and well regarded amongst their colleagues for their substantial contribution to many areas of Probability, Statistics and Stochastic Analysis during their lifetime. To honour their memory, the Chris Heyde & Joe Gani Scholarship has been established at the ANU to enable students to study and expand research into these fields. The Scholarships are funded by the interest on contributions from friends, colleagues, family and the ANU Endowment for Excellence. Two Scholarships will be offered annually subject to funds beings available.
records.eligibility: a domestic and/or international student; enrolled in a program of study leading to the award of a PhD; undertaking research in areas of probability, statistical science or stochastic analysis.

records.title: Florence McKenzie Chair
records.description: Each year the School of Cybernetics in the ANU College of Engineering and Computer Science (College) may offer up to 10 awards known as the FMK Supplementary Scholarship (Award). Funding for this Award has been provided by the Florence Violet McKenzie Chair. The Australian National University (ANU) College of Engineering and Computer Science is embarking on an ambitious agenda to reimagine engineering and computing to launch our society into the middle of the 21st Century. We are bringing non-traditional skills to engineering and computing to put people in the centre of delivering solutions to global challenges.
records.eligibility: Have received a statement of support from the SOCY cohort PhD program convenor; are enrolled full-time in the cohort program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy at SOCY at the ANU; have been awarded, and continue to hold, an ANU approved PhD base stipend scholarship; have agreed to assign the ownership of any Student Material (as defined in the Student Assignment and Confidentiality Deed (Deed)) including any Intellectual Property embodied in the Student Material to the University, in accordance with the terms of the Deed between the recipient and the University. The recipient is encouraged to seek independent advice before signing the Deed and accepting this Award, for example via the ANU Postgraduate & Research Students' Association (PARSA).

records.title: System-Level Multiphase Flow and Bubble Transport for Efficient Electrochemical Hydrogen Production
records.description: We are seeking a PhD candidate to investigate system-level multiphase flow processes in electrochemical hydrogen production. The project will focus on how operating conditions, porous transport layers, electrode properties, and gas bubble transport influence hydrogen and oxygen generation in water electrolysis systems. Efficient removal of gas bubbles is critical to the performance of electrochemical hydrogen production devices. Bubbles generated during water electrolysis can block active reaction sites, increase electrical resistance, disturb liquid flow and mass transport, and reduce overall production efficiency. At the system level, these effects are governed by coupled interactions between electrochemical operation, multiphase flow, porous media transport, surface wettability, temperature, and flow conditions. This project will investigate these coupled processes to identify practical strategies for improving electrolyser performance.
records.eligibility: Completion of a Bachelor (Honours) or Master by Research degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, applied mathematics, applied physics or related disciplines

records.title: QUT-CSIRO PhD Scholarship in Deep Learning for Hyperspectral Image Classification
records.description: Hyperspectral imaging is one of the rapidly growing domains in remote sensing primarily due to the breadth of applications on a variety of areas, from plant disease detection to object tracking. For example, hyperspectral imaging provides an opportunity to develop fast and non-invasive methods of detecting plant diseases and potentially discriminating between different disease types (e.g. virus, fungus, bacteria) before the human eye can see them. The principal aim of this PhD research program is to develop methods to improve the hyperspectral image classification using deep learning techniques. The developed systems will be evaluated on their ability to detect plant diseases and potentially discriminating between different disease types using the hyperspectral imaging dataset which has been already collected by CSIRO.
records.eligibility: You must: meet QUT’s PhD admission criteria (Degree in Electrical Engineering and/or Computer Science with first class honours). We would like you to have: sound knowledge of machine learning, computer vision and image processing, strong programming skills.
records.amount_comment: A scholarship between $37,000 and $40,000 per year for 3 years (consisting of a base stipend of $27,000 and a top-up between $10,000 and $13,000) with a possible extension of 6 months. Up to $5,000 per year for project costs (to be agreed between CSIRO and QUT on a case by case basis). Additional funding for project costs up to a further $5,000 per year may also be available, if required, from CSIRO on a case by case basis.

records.description: Scholarships are awarded on the basis of academic excellence and research potential to local and international candidates undertaking a research doctoral degree.
records.eligibility: Applicants must: be Australian or New Zealand citizens, Australian permanent residents or international candidates; be commencing in an RMIT PhD program; have completed a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours; and have applied for a full-time PhD program at RMIT. Part-time VCPS may be approved for candidates with exceptional circumstances (e.g. for medical reasons or due to significant care commitments). Part-time scholarships are not tax exempt. Applicants will be considered ineligible for a VCPS if: they are currently holding a research doctorate, or an equivalent research qualification; currently undertaking a research doctorate; or currently receiving another equivalent award, scholarship or research related salary providing a benefit greater than 75 per cent of the current year APA base rate to undertake the research degree.More information on research grants: https://www.rmit.edu.au/students/careers-opportunities/scholarships/researchResearch contact details: https://www.rmit.edu.au/research/contact/contact-the-school-of-graduate-research
records.amount_comment: a stipend of $47,821 per annum pro rata (full-time study) which represents a generous RMIT top-up of approximately $12,000 above the RTP rate; a research support allowance of $5,000 per annum to support research activities; International candidates in receipt of this scholarship are also awarded an RMIT Research International Tuition Fee Scholarship (RRITFS); All local candidates, Australian and New Zealand citizens or permanent residents of Australia are provided with an RTP Fee Offset scholarship. Applicants in receipt of an RTP Fee Offset scholarship are not required to pay tuition fees for the maximum duration of their candidature; a relocation allowance for the cost of relocating in order to take up their postgraduate research program, up to $515 per adult and $255 per child to a maximum of $1,540; paid sick, maternity and parenting leave (within the limits of the Scholarship Terms and Conditions); if you are an international candidate, you will also receive the cost of an Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) policy for your visa duration.

records.title: Foundation Scholarships (Humanitarian)
records.description: Foundation Scholarships are awarded for entry into our School at Year 7 and Years 9 – 11 at either Caulfield Campus or Wheelers Hill Campus. Foundation Scholarships are awarded, utilising needs based criteria, to provide opportunities for those who would otherwise be unable to access a Caulfield Grammar School education. Recipients generally come from backgrounds that are underrepresented at our School. The current focus of the Foundation Scholarships is on students from Indigenous and refugee backgrounds. While we work closely with Indigenous and refugee communities across Victoria to identify students who would thrive in our School environment and have the strong support of their family, we welcome applications. Foundation Scholarship recipients will demonstrate sound academic ability, achievement in several fields of endeavour, including leadership, and show a desire to contribute to the Caulfield Grammar School community.

records.title: Future Crops Centre Scholarship
records.description: The ARC Training Centre for Future Crops is working directly with industry and the community to train the next generation of research and industry leaders to deliver impactful projects with real-world implications for food security. Students in plant science and communication in science will have opportunities to engage with industry partners and communities on projects to improve the yield and nutritional value of the crops that underpin the energy and protein content of the human diet. Together, the Centre will build future R&D capabilities in the Agrifood sector to drive growth, productivity and competitiveness for the benefit of agriculture and global food security. These scholarships will enable students to pursue a PhD program conducting research that is either a core project within the Centre, or closely aligns with the strategic directions of the Centre, based in the College of Science.
records.eligibility: is enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy, based in the ANU College of Science; has been awarded a first-class honours or equivalent; is undertaking one of the core Centre PhD research projects, or a project approved by the Centre Executive.

records.title: JCSMR Gender Equity Fund
records.description: Each year the John Curtin School of Medical Research (the JCSMR) in the ANU College of Health & Medicine may offer funding of up to $10,000 from the JCSMR Gender Equity Fund. Funding has been provided by a generous initial donation by Professor Carola Vinuesa and continues with the support of Richard Miller and the School, as funding permits. The objective of this Fund is to provide funding for an early or mid-career researcher or domestic or international PhD student who is experiencing significant career disruption resulting from the birth of a child, or the primary care of a child, which limits or prevents their career progression and research activities in the John Curtin School of Medical Research.
records.eligibility: a female-identifying researcher at the JCSMR who holds a current academic appointment at level A-C and intends to return to a career in research; a continuing domestic or international female-identifying student who is enrolled in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy, based in the John Curtin School of Medical Research (the JCSMR) and, in relation to the birth or care of a child,; is experiencing a period of significant career disruption (generally at least 12 weeks) or expects to do so within the next 6 months; within the last 12 months, has applied for or returned from a period of career disruption (generally at least 12 weeks).

records.title: John Willett International Scholarship

In memory of Professor Willett's work in management education, particularly in Asia, a fund was established to provide a scholarship for students from selected countries in Asia within the Griffith Business School, formerly the Graduate School of Management. The John Willett International Scholarship will offer a 50% tuition fee waiver for a maximum period of two years for the selected recipient to complete their Master of Global Development at Griffith. This will provide an opportunity for the recipient to acquire knowledge and skills needed to promote global sustainable development.

records.title: STEM Accommodation Scholarship
records.description: Enjoy a stress-free start to your studies and save up to $15,500 with the unique STEM Accommodation Scholarship at Victoria University (VU). Our exciting merit-based scholarship offers eligible international students free accommodation at UniLodge Victoria University for up to your entire first year of study. Scholarships will be awarded to select offshore international applicants for science, engineering and information technology degrees offered at VU Melbourne, particularly at our Footscray Park Campus, the main hub of our STEM-related courses. Limited scholarships are available for the July and September intakes in 2025, as well as February 2026. Eligibility is assessed on merit, based on previous academic results. With scholarships awarded on a first-come, first-served basis to eligible students, apply now for the best chance of success!
records.eligibility: In order to be eligible for this scholarship, you must be an international student applying to VU from outside Australia and meet the entry requirements for one of the following STEM-related course:; Bachelor of Architectural Design; Bachelor of Biomedical Science; Bachelor of Biomedical and Exercise Science; Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours); Bachelor of Cyber Security; Bachelor of Data Science; Bachelor of Dermal Sciences; Bachelor of Information Technology; Bachelor of Information Technology (Professional); Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Civil Engineering); Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Electrical and Electronic Engineering); Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Mechanical Engineering); Bachelor of Exercise Science (Clinical Practice); Bachelor of Exercise Science (Sport Practice); Bachelor of Health Science; Bachelor of Sport Science; Bachelor of Sport Science (Human Movement) / Bachelor of Sport Management; Bachelor of Sport Science (Human Movement) / Bachelor of Psychological Studies; Master of Applied Information Technology; Master of Clinical Exercise Science and Rehabilitation; Master of Construction Management; Master of Project Management; Priority will be given to applicants with a strong academic background. Limited scholarships are available for Semester 2, Block 1 (July), 2025, Semester 2, Block 3 (September), 2025, and Semester 1, Block 1 (February), 2026, so apply as soon as you can; We strongly encourage applications from female students as part of our commitment to closing the gender gap in STEM. Please note: you must be over 18 years old when you start your VU studies in order to be eligible for this scholarship.

records.title: Curtin English Language Program Scholarship
records.description: In collaboration with Curtin University, Curtin College offers an English Language Program subsidy worth up to AUD$7,008 towards Curtin English courses.
records.eligibility: You must be an international, full fee-paying, student who has received a conditional offer (subject to meeting English) to study at Curtin. This Scholarship is not available to Australian citizens or Permanent Residents. You must be undertaking an English Language Program to meet your English Requirement. You must not have met Curtin’s English language requirements for entry into your Mainstream Course and must commence your Mainstream Course at Curtin’s Perth campus in-person or fully online within one year after successfully completing the English Language Program to meet the requirements. You must be studying a full-time undergraduate degree, postgraduate degree by coursework or Higher Degree by Research program of at least 1 year and for a minimum of 200 credit points. You must pay upfront the fees associated with all your English Language Programs PLUS a AUD$1,000 deposit (the Deposit) at the time you accept the packaged offer contained in your Letter of Offer (different requirements apply to Sponsored students – see further below): Curtin will credit the AUD$1,000 Deposit AND the Scholarship of up to AUD$7,008 towards your tuition fee account for use in the second semester of your Mainstream course. If you do not continue to the Mainstream Course (whether you chose to withdraw or due to not meeting the English Requirement), the AUD$1,000 Deposit will be non-refundable. Once you successfully complete your English course, in order to be admitted into your mainstream course, you are required to pay the full Deposit tuition fee of the mainstream course as indicated on the letter of offer. You must progress to your Mainstream Course and maintain your enrolment as an international, full fee-paying, student for at least one semester of your Mainstream Course. If you do not, then the Scholarship will be cancelled and you will not receive the Scholarship either in the form of a credit or refund of the tuition fees for your English Language Program (unless you qualify for any exceptions under the Curtin English Refund Policy). If your English Language Program costs less than the Scholarship, you cannot apply the Scholarship to any other international student expense or claim any remaining portion of the Scholarship. The Scholarship will only be applied to tuition, and enrolment fees. Curtin will not reissue this offer if you have to extend your English Language Program due to unsuccessful English academic progression. If you are unsuccessful in your initial English Language Program, you must pay for any further English courses you choose to study. You cannot spend the Scholarship or cash it in for any other purpose. This offer will not be extended beyond its prescribed duration or amount unless notified otherwise by Curtin in writing. This offer will not be extended beyond its prescribed duration or amount unless notified otherwise by Curtin in writing. This offer cannot be transferred to a Curtin campus or partner outside Western Australia, or to another university or educational institution. Curtin can cancel this offer if you do not accept your Letter of Offer or enrol in your Mainstream Course by the date specified. If you are a Sponsored student, different requirements apply

records.title: PhD Scholarship - Solvent-Based Direct Lithium Extraction
records.description: This three-year PhD project, part of the ARC Industrial Transformation Research Hub for Critical Energy Separation Materials (ARC CREST), will develop an innovative and sustainable pathway for lithium recovery by coupling α-spodumene processing with downstream solvent-based direct lithium extraction (DLE). The research will focus on optimising lithium extraction and purification, understanding the effects of feedstock properties and impurities, and integrating the processes into an efficient flowsheet. The project offers multidisciplinary experience in critical mineral processing, hydrometallurgy, solvent extraction, materials characterisation, and process optimisation.
records.eligibility: This position is open to domestic and international candidates. records.title: Bridging the distance: Using sport technology to enhance high-performance pathways for rural athletes
records.description: Overarching Aim of the PhD:Athletes from regional and rural Australia face significant barriers in accessing high-performance sport pathways, including limited access to coaching, sport science support, and elite competition environments. Advances in sport technology (e.g., wearable sensors, remote coaching platforms, performance analytics) offer an opportunity to overcome these geographic constraints.This PhD project will design, implement, and evaluate technology-enabled athlete development models to support regional athletes in achieving high-performance outcomes without the need for relocation.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the project, you must:; be eligible for a PhD; willing to undertake full-time study

records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing international student at a Monash Campus in Australia, in one of the below courses:; P2001 Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Science or P3002 Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Science Advanced (Honours); P6005** Master of Pharmaceutical Science; P6006 Master of Global Medicines Development; P6007 Pharmacy (Honours) Scholars Program/Doctor of Pharmacy
records.amount_comment: 50% of tuition fees paid per year until the minimum credit points for your degree are completed (awarded to the highest achieving student in each of the four course groups nominated).; 25% of tuition fees paid per year until the minimum credit points for your degree are completed (awarded to the second highest achieving student in each of the four course groups nominated).

records.title: Klaus Abbink Honours Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded in memory of Klaus Abbink, a Professor in Economics at Monash and a Director of The Monash Laboratory for Experimental Economics (MonLEE). Professor Abbink was regarded as a great supervisor and teacher for his students, always passing on his exceptional critical thinking and research principles. He was very patient and provided consistent care and equal effort for everyone that crossed his path.
records.eligibility: A student commencing a Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) or Bachelor of Economics (Honours) in the Monash Business School at a Monash campus in Australia.; WAM 80+ (Direct entry International students)

records.title: The Koto Dream Scholarship
records.description: The Koto Dream Scholarship is designed to support outstanding Know One, Teaching One (KOTO) alumni who demonstrate strong academic potential, leadership capacity, and a clear commitment to social impact, enabling them to pursue undergraduate studies at Monash University overseas. This scholarship reflects Monash University's commitment to equity, access to education, and global social impact, while empowering first-generation learners from disadvantaged backgrounds to become future changemakers in their communities.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; An alumni of Know One, Teaching One (KOTO).; Commencing student intending to enrol full-time in an undergraduate degree at a Monash campus in Australia; Must be enrolled in one of the following areas:; Business, Management, and Economics; Communication, Media, and Social Sciences; Sustainability, Development Studies, or related disciplines
records.amount_comment: 100% tuition sponsorship for course duration (maximum of three years)

records.title: Monash International Merit Scholarship
records.description: International students from all countries who have received an undergraduate course offer from Monash will automatically be considered for the Monash International Merit Scholarship. As a scholarship recipient, you will receive $15,000 per annum for the duration of your degree.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; You must have received a full Monash course offer with no conditions; You must intend to enrol full-time in an undergraduate degree at a Monash campus in Australia; You are not eligible for this scholarship if you are:; a current Monash student; studying an Australian Year 12. You may be eligible for the Sir John Monash Scholarship for Excellence.; commencing in the Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine (MD).; in Monash Pathway programs (e.g. Monash College and Monash University Foundation Year).; transferring from another Monash campus or applying to Monash from another Australian University.
records.amount_comment: $15,000 per annum (48 credit points of study) paid per year until the minimum number of points for your degree is completed (For scholarships awarded from 2026).; $10,000 per annum (48 credit points of study) paid per year until the minimum number of points for your degree is completed (For scholarships awarded pre 2026).

records.title: Master of Applied Econometrics PHD Pathway Scholarship
records.description: Are you passionate about econometric model building, estimation and forecasting for economic decision-making ? Elevate your career in economics with the Master of Applied Econometrics (with PhD pathway) scholarship. This prestigious opportunity is designed for aspiring professionals who seek to deepen their skills in econometrics and make a real impact in academia, industry, or public policy. Our scholarship offers financial support to exceptional candidates, allowing you to focus on gaining expertise in advanced econometric techniques, data modelling, and statistical analysis. The Master of Applied Econometrics program combines rigorous coursework with hands-on experience, equipping you with the tools to tackle complex economic and financial issues, and contribute to the policy making process.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing or continuing student enrolled in the Master of Applied Econometrics (PHD pathway) in the Department of Econometrics & Business Statistics in the Faculty of Business and Economics at the Monash Clayton campus.; WAM 80+ (Direct entry International students).

records.title: MD-PhD Industry Leaders Scholarship (for returning MD-PhD students)
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to Monash University medical students who have demonstrated a commitment to becoming a clinician scientist by undertaking the Monash University intercalated MD-PhD pathway. The successful recipients must have been enrolled in their PhD through one of the Schools that is supporting this Scholarship*, and must have submitted their PhD thesis and returned to complete the final year of the Monash University medical degree.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Current student enrolled in and commenced the final year (Year 5/D) of the Clayton BMedSc/MD degree (M6011 or M6018) in the Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences as a Monash Campus in Australia.; You must have completed BMedSc(Hons) M3701 and achieved an 80 WAM or above.; You must have undertaken the MD-PhD pathway at Monash University through one of the MNHS Schools supporting this Scholarship* AND submitted their PhD thesis for examination.
records.amount_comment: $15,000 to be paid to students who submit their PhD thesis before the FY32 census date in the year that they return to their BMedSc/MD degree.; $7,500 to be paid to students who submit their PhD thesis between the FY32 census date and the Semester 2 census date in the year that they return to their BMedSc/MD degree.

records.title: Master of Commerce Scholarship
records.description: The Master of Commerce is a research-oriented programme preparing students for a PhD and an academic career. Offered as part of an Integrated PhD program, the MCom may be completed in one or two years, depending on the specialisation and the student's prior studies. The MCom provides advanced coursework relevant to the specialisation to provide a thorough academic grounding in the skills and knowledge required to undertake original research. Upon successful completion of the MCom degree, students who perform at the required standard and demonstrate strong research capability will progress to the PhD (3 years). The MCom is the perfect pathway to doctoral studies for students who aim to pursue an academic career.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; A current full-time Monash student or an applicant seeking to enrol full-time, in the Master of Commerce degree; You are not eligible for this scholarship if you are, or become, employed on a continuing basis or a fixed term contract for 3 months or greater.
records.amount_comment: Tuition fees paid, plus an allowance of $37,145 (the equivalent to the 2026 PhD stipend rate).

records.title: Skilled Industry Placement Scholarship
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Enrolled in BRM5022 Biotechnology work-integrated learning.
records.amount_comment: $14,300 paid in three instalments.; 24 week placement with one of the host sites in the SKILLED clinical trials internships program.

records.title: Finance Honours Grant
records.description: This scholarship supports academically outstanding students undertaking the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) majoring in Finance.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing full-time in the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) (B3701) degree majoring in finance at a Monash University campus in Australia.
records.amount_comment: $6000 one-off payment.

records.title: Vice-Chancellor International School Leaver Award
records.description: The Monash Vice Chancellor School Leavers Award for International Students celebrates high-achieving international students enrolling in an undergraduate (coursework) degree at a Monash campus in Australia.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing student enrolled in an undergraduate degree at a Monash campus in Australia.; ATAR of 83 and above to be considered; You must have received a Monash course offer.

records.title: International Futures Scholarship - 2027
records.description: Murdoch is offering a 20% fee reduction scholarship for International students enrolled in eligible courses commencing in 2027.
records.eligibility: You are eligible to receive this scholarship if you meet all the following requirements:; you are an international, full-fee-paying student.; you are starting studies at one of Murdoch’s Western Australian campuses in 2027.; you are starting studies for an eligible Murdoch coursework degree set out below.; you are not receiving any other Murdoch scholarship.; you are not subject to any of the exceptions set out below.
records.amount_comment: 20% tuition fee reduction

records.title: International Welcome Scholarship 2028
records.description: Murdoch is offering a 15% fee reduction scholarship for international students from eligible countries, commencing in 2028.
records.eligibility: You are eligible to receive this scholarship if you meet all the following requirements:; you are an international, full fee paying student; you are starting studies at one of Murdoch's Western Australian campuses in 2028; you are starting studies for an eligible Murdoch coursework degree set out below; you are a citizen of one of the eligible countries set out below; you are not receiving any other Murdoch scholarship.
records.amount_comment: 15% tuition fee reduction

records.title: Investigation on Bubble Dynamics Under Electric Fields in Water Electrolysis Process
records.description: We are seeking a PhD candidate to investigate gas bubble dynamics under the influence of electric fields, with a particular focus on applications in electrochemical hydrogen production. The project will examine the physical mechanisms governing bubble generation, growth, detachment, coalescence, and transport near electrode surfaces, with the aim of improving bubble removal and enhancing the efficiency of water electrolysis systems.
records.eligibility: Completion of a Bachelor (Honours) or Master by Research degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, applied mathematics, applied physics or related disciplines

records.title: A smart CPR feedback device for cardiac arrest (PhD scholarship)
records.description: This PhD project focuses on developing the first-ever closed-loop cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) feedback device. The device uses non-invasive sensors to measure blood oxygenation in the brain and tells the CPR provider how to adjust their compression depth, rate, and release to improve patient outcomes. The student will have the opportunity to work with a range of engineers, doctors, and paramedics and will help to develop this prototype into an ambulance-ready device, ready for deployment in large-scale clinical trials.
records.eligibility: You need to meet the entry requirements for QUT's Doctor of Philosophy, including any English language requirements.; Enrol as a full-time, internal student.; Have a background in electrical, mechatronic, or biomedical engineering, expertise in biosensors or optics. Should be comfortable being hands-on. Requires experience in circuit design and microcontroller programming.

records.title: Tuition Fee Sponsorship (TFS) for research students
records.description: A sponsorship to help international student pay tuition fees.
records.eligibility: International students who enrol in a QUT research degree and are in receipt of:; a stipend scholarship awarded by QUT; a stipend scholarship funded by an organisation with which QUT has an external agreement to sponsor fees for this student or relevant cohort of students.; Candidates will not be eligible if they receive another tuition fees offset or sponsorship from any source, including QUT.; You cannot apply for a Tuition Fee Sponsorship - your eligibility is reviewed via your application for admission.

records.title: Fast Track University Pathway Academic Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship provides financial assistance to high achieving Fast Track University Pathway international students.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; have existing offer letter (full or conditional offer) and be a commencing student in Semester 2 2027 intake in any stream of Fast Track University Pathways program
records.amount_comment: The total value of the scholarship is a AU$5,000, one-off payment towards future tuition fees to be paid after the first census date into student's university account.

records.title: Future Leaders Scholarship
records.description: Provides students from India and the subcontinent with a 20% tuition fee reduction for eligible Bachelor and Masters programs that have received an offer from 2026.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal or Pakistan (including dual citizenship holding one of these country's passport); be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; have an offer letter to commence from 2026 intakes onwards in one of the following programs at RMIT: Bachelor degree, Masters by Coursework; not be an existing student who commence in another program within the same study level
records.amount_comment: The value of the scholarship is a 20% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the eligible program(s)* as outlined in your offer letter.

records.title: Medibank Excellence Scholarship
records.description: The Medibank Excellence Scholarship is available to international students studying Australian Year 12 or International Baccalaureate in Australia. In addition to receiving AU$12,000 successful applicants will have the opportunity to attend Medibank workshops, participate in event-coordination for Medibank on Open Day, meet recent graduates working at Medibank, and be involved in a customer focus group.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship, you must:; be applying from Australia; be a current year 12 student in Australia graduating in 2026; be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; submit your application via VTAC and receive an offer from RMIT for an Associate degree or Undergraduate degree; not be an existing RMIT student.
records.amount_comment: The total value of the scholarship is AU$12,000, to be paid to recipient's Australian bank account in AU$6,000 installments after the census date of each semester of the first year.

records.title: RMIT UP Academic English Bursary for Latin America, Spain and Türkiye
records.description: If you are a citizen of a Latin American country, Spain or Türkiye this bursary provides a tuition fee discount on your Academic English course.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Latin America countries, Spain or Türkiye; applying from Australia or overseas; enrol in an Academic English course at RMIT University Pathways (RMIT UP) commencing in 2026 or 2027; be a commencing RMIT UP student (including extending your program in Australia).
records.amount_comment: 35% of the total program fee for an Academic English course (you pay $355 per week after the discount); 40% of the total program fee for an Academic English course (you pay $339 per week after the discount)

records.title: RMIT UP IELTS Preparation Bursary for Asia
records.description: If you are a citizen of Japan, South Korea, Taiwan or Thailand this bursary provides a tuition fee discount on your IELTS Preparation course.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be citizen of Japan, South Korea, Taiwan or Thailand; be applying from Australia or overseas; enrol in an IELTS Preparation course at RMIT University Pathways (RMIT UP) commencing in 2026 or 2027 for 10 weeks or more; not be the recipient of any other English Language scholarship (including external scholarships); be a commencing RMIT UP student (including extending your course in Australia).

records.title: RMIT University Top-up Scholarship for Vietnam Government (Project 89)
records.description: This top-up scholarship program is available to talented Vietnamese students aims to address Vietnam's future industry and workforce needs, prioritising key research areas such as digital technologies, physics, biotechnologies and energy & environment.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Vietnam; have an offer for a PhD program at RMIT; be nominated to receive the Vietnam government scholarship (Project 89); commence full-time enrolment as an onshore international student at RMIT in Melbourne
records.amount_comment: a tuition fee scholarship of up to $25,000 USD; a stipend scholarship of $1,120 USD per month; an international return airfare and travel allowances; Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the time spent in Australia (up to $1,000 USD per year).

records.title: Student Opportunities Fund
records.description: Southern Cross University is committed to helping provide exceptional students with exceptional opportunities to broaden their professional networks and opportunities. The Southern Cross Student Opportunities Fund will provide students with the opportunity to apply for a scholarship worth up to $7,500 each to help subsidise the cost of travel, accommodation and necessary activities to help them realise their full professional potential.
records.eligibility: Please note that this scholarship is only available to students who have progressed their opportunity to such a point that its occurrence is almost certain. As such, students may have to purchase tickets or accommodation in advance of being awarded this scholarship, in which case, the scholarship panel will consider the costs already incurred and include that in their deliberations as to the amount granted if successful. The strength of each application will be measured against the above selection criteria. A report will make recommendations to the selection panel, which will be represented by the Office of Engagement, Office of Research, Finance, Governance and other work units where specialist insights may be required.

records.title: International Women's Day Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship will support a current student to continue to achieve outstandingly in her studies. The scholarship will form part of the celebrations of International Women’s Day. International Women’s Day celebrates and acknowledges the achievements of women globally on 8 March each year.
records.eligibility: This scholarship will support a current student to continue to achieve outstandingly in her studies. The scholarship will form part of the celebrations of International Women’s Day. International Women’s Day celebrates and acknowledges the achievements of women globally on 8 March each year.

records.title: Macquarie University College $5,000 Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to all eligible students who are commencing a Diploma degree at the Macquarie University College.
records.eligibility: Be an international full fee-paying student. Be a citizen of Bangladesh, Iran, Nepal, Turkey, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, Mongolia, or Uzbekistan. Be commencing full-time in a Diploma Program at Macquarie University College in T4 2026 and beyond. Accept your Letter of Offer and pay the commencement fee by the Acceptance Deadline.

records.title: Macquarie University $10,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship offers talented international students from eligible countries AUD $10,000 per year towards their studies at Macquarie University. The scholarship is applied throughout the duration of an eligible Bachelor's and Master's coursework degree, with AUD $5,000 credited each session.

Be commencing full-time in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Macquarie University in 2027 and beyond (excluding Graduate Certificates, Bachelor of Clinical Science, Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours), Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Physiotherapy, Master of Clinical Audiology, Master of Clinical Psychology, Master of Clinical Neuropsychology, Master of Organisational Psychology, Master of Professional Psychology, Master of Speech and Language Pathology). records.title: Macquarie University $15,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship offers talented international students from Vietnam, Indonesia and the Philippines AUD $15,000 per year towards their studies at Macquarie University. Valued among the most generous scholarships in Australia, the scholarship is available for the full duration of an eligible Bachelor's and Master's coursework degree commencing from 2027, with AUD $7,500 credited each session.

Accept your Letter of Offer and pay the commencement fee by the Acceptance Deadline. Must not be a recipient of a government sponsorship or scholarship that covers full tuition fees, unless approved by Macquarie University Scholarships Team. Please note: The annual number of scholarship recipients may vary according to the availability of funding and the number of eligible candidates and will only be confirmed when an offer letter is made.
records.amount_comment: This scholarship is valid for the full duration of the course.

records.title: Partner Institution Scholarship
records.description: To recognise the strong relationship between Macquarie University and its partner institutions, the Partner Institution Scholarship is awarded to high performing prospective students with a quest for knowledge. The competitive scholarship is valued up to AUD $15,000 per year for talented students who are currently studying at a partner institution and are transferring to study at Macquarie University (AUD $7,500 will be credited each session). For India and South Asia region students, the first payment of AUD $15,000 will be credited in the second session of their first year of enrolment, with AUD $7,500 credited in each subsequent session for the duration of the course.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the scholarship, applicants must meet the following criteria: Be an international full fee-paying student. Be commencing full-time in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Macquarie University in 2027 and beyond (excluding Graduate Certificates, Bachelor of Clinical Science, Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours), Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Physiotherapy, Master of Clinical Audiology, Master of Clinical Psychology, Master of Clinical Neuropsychology, Master of Organisational Psychology, Master of Professional Psychology, Master of Speech and Language Pathology). Transfer from a Macquarie University partner institution. Achieve a minimum 65 WAM for postgraduate or a minimum 85 ATAR (or equivalent) for undergraduate applications. Must not have received a scholarship or sponsorship from Macquarie University or another organisation for the degree (unless stated otherwise by the Scholarship Committee). Commence study in the session and year indicated in your scholarship letter of offer. Please note: The annual number of scholarship recipients may vary according to the availability of funding and the number of eligible candidates and will only be confirmed when an offer letter is made.
records.amount_comment: This scholarship is valid for the full duration of the course. AUD $7,500 will be credited each session.

records.title: Stanley Liebich Memorial Scholarship 2027
records.description: The Stanley Liebich Memorial Scholarship was first established in December 1940, in memory of the late Stanley Ormond Crossley Liebich. This scholarship supports a student from a disadvantaged background enrolled in the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) degree, who progressed from the Associate Degree in Engineering OR Advanced Diploma of Engineering Technology.
records.eligibility: Applicants must:; have progressed from the Associate Degree in Engineering OR Advanced Diploma of Engineering Technology prior to Bachelor of Engineering course.

records.title: Swinburne Research Stipend Scholarships
records.description: Swinburne Research Stipend (SRS) scholarships are awarded to candidates of exceptional research potential undertaking doctoral studies. The awards are provided to assist with general living costs. Successful scholarship applicants are automatically awarded a RTP Fees-Offset (Domestic) Scholarship (domestic students) or a Tuition Fee Scholarship (international students) which covers tuition fees for up to four years.
records.eligibility: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Professional Doctorate

records.title: Research Training Program Stipend - RTP Stipend
records.description: Research Training Program (RTP) Stipend scholarships are awarded to candidates of exceptional research potential, enrolled in a Higher Degree by Research (HDR) course of study, to assist with general living costs. These scholarships are available to both future and current students enrolled in or applying for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Professional Doctorate course at Swinburne.
records.eligibility: Please refer to the Swinburne Research Stipend Scholarship webpage.

records.title: Alexander McTaggart Honours Scholarship
records.description: Each year, the John Curtin School of Medical Research (JCSMR) within the ANU College of Science and Medicine at the Australian National University (ANU) may offer an award known as the Alexander McTaggart Memorial Scholarship. The objective of the Award is to support a student undertaking their Honours project at the John Curtin School of Medical Research, with the research to be conducted in a field related to cancer research and allied subjects. Funding for this Award has been provided in the memory of its donor, Mr Alexander McTaggart.
records.eligibility: The scholarship is available to an applicant:; who is an international or domestic student; who is enrolled in an Honours year at the John Curtin School of Medical Research; whose Honours project is related to cancer research and allied fields.

records.title: Dr Matthew Valetich Honours Scholarship in Geoscience
records.description: Each year, the Research School of Earth Sciences within the ANU College of Science and Medicine may offer an award known as the Dr Matthew Valetich Honours Scholarship in Geoscience. The objective of the Award is to provide financial assistance to a student undertaking their honours year in geoscience. Funding for this Award has been provided by Anglo American Exploration (Australia) Pty Limited in honour of Dr Matthew Valetich, a PhD graduate of the Research School of Earth Sciences.
records.eligibility: The Award is available each year to a commencing or continuing ANU student who:; is a domestic or international student; receives an offer of admission to a Bachelor of Science (Honours), Bachelor of Philosophy (Honours), or Bachelor of Science (Advanced) (Honours) program within the ANU College of Science and Medicine; is enrolled in an Honours research project based in the Research School of Earth Sciences (RSES). Supervision by staff from other ANU research schools within the ANU College of Science and Medicine is permitted and encouraged; can demonstrate financial hardship that may impact their ability to commence, continue, or complete their studies.

records.title: The Friends of the ANU Classics Museum Grant for Collection Research
records.description: Each year the School of Literature, Languages and Linguistics may offer an award known as The Friends of the ANU Classics Museum Grant for Collection Research. The objective of the Award is to support Honours and Master's students in one of the eligible specialisations listed below whose thesis research will include the study of objects in the collection of the ANU Classics Museum, especially their provenance and collection history.
records.eligibility: The Award is available each year to a commencing or continuing ANU student who:; is a domestic or international student; receives an offer of admission to an Honours program or a Master’s program at the ANU College of Arts and Social Sciences in one of the following fields:; Classical Studies; Archaeology; Anthropology; Art History and Theory; History; Middle Eastern and Central Asian Studies; Museums and Collections; Museum Education and Heritage Interpretation; Intangible Cultural Heritage; any other field deemed relevant by the Selection Committee; will conduct research on the provenance and/or collection history of objects in the ANU Classics Museum.

records.title: Samuel Crawcour Bursaries
records.description: The Samuel Crawcour Bursaries was established by the late Samuel Crawcour and is offered to medicine students who experience disadvantaged circumstances.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this bursary, you must:; Be enrolled in the Doctor of Medicine; Demonstrate financial hardship

records.title: Grathelms Piano Award
records.description: The Grathelms Piano Award was established with a gift from Neil McGrath and is offered to talented students enrolled in the Bachelor of Music (Performance) or Master of Music (Music Performance) specialising in Piano who are experiencing immediate disadvantaged circumstances. Preference is given to students who are commencing the penultimate or final year of their degree.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this award, you must:; Be enrolled in the Bachelor of Music (Performance) or Master of Music (Music Performance) (or their successors) and specialising in Piano.

records.title: RD Phillips Bursary
records.description: The RD Phillips Bursary was established with a gift from Royal Daniel Phillips and is awarded to students who are enrolled in the Doctor of Medicine and are experiencing immediate financial disadvantage.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this bursary, you must be enrolled in the Doctor of Medicine.

records.title: David Ashton Scholarship
records.description: The David Ashton Scholarship is supported by the Melbourne Botany Foundation and is offered to high-achieving graduate researchers who are enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy in the Faculty of Science and undertaking research in the field of Botany.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Be enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy in the Faculty of Science and be undertaking research in Botany in the School of Biosciences (or its successor); Have achieved academic results at Honours 2A level or above (or equivalent).

records.title: Lionel Gell Screen Production Bursary
records.description: The Lionel Gell Screen Production Bursary was established with a gift from the Lionel Gell Foundation and is offered to students who are producing high-quality, industry-standard graduation films as part of their final year of a degree in Film and Television and are experiencing financial need. Preference is given to high-achieving students.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this bursary, you must be enrolled in the final year of the Bachelor of Fine Arts (Film and Television), Bachelor of Fine Arts (Degree with Honours) (Film and Television) or Master of Film and Television (either year).

records.title: State Music Camp Victoria Award
records.description: The State Music Camp Victoria Award was established with a gift from the State Music Camp Victoria Limited and is offered to students who attended the camp and demonstrated a high standard of musicality and potential to further develop their conducting skills.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this award, you must be enrolled as a Master of Music (Performance Teaching) or PhD student in Music (specialising in conducting) in the Faculty of Fine Arts and Music.

records.title: Maureen Brunt Scholarship
records.description: The Maureen Brunt scholarship is offered to talented graduates of economics and who are undertaking study in an overseas university for a postgraduate degree or diploma in economics or in a field with a major component of economics.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Have completed, or be completing, a degree in Economics at the University of Melbourne in 2026. This includes: BCom students who are majoring in Economics, BCom Honours students who are majoring in Economics, Master of Economics or Master of Commerce (Economics) students, PhD Economics students; Be intending to undertake study in Economics, or in a field with a major component of Economics, at an overseas university for a postgraduate coursework or research degree or diploma.; Have a letter of offer from an overseas institution to commence a postgraduate coursework or research degree in Economics or in a field with a major component of Economics.

records.title: John S Turner Postgraduate Scholarship
records.description: The John S Turner Postgraduate Scholarship is supported by the School of Botany Foundation and is offered to graduate researchers who are enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy (Science) and undertaking research in the field of plant physiology, plant ecology or conservation plant biology.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Be enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy in the discipline of Botany within the School of BioSciences; Undertaking research in the field of plant physiology, plant ecology or conservation plant biology

records.title: Notre Dame Australia International Scholarship Master of Social Work (Qualifying).
records.description: The University of Notre Dame Australia (University) offers the International Scholarship Master of Social Work (Qualifying) to provide tuition assistance to international students enrolling in the Master of Social Work (Qualifying).
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the Scholarship, students must:; Be international full fee-paying students commencing a Master of Social Work (Qualifying) program for the first time at The University of Notre Dame Australia; Have accepted an Offer of Admission (by the relevant deadline) and satisfied any admission requirements to study the CRICOS registered Master of Social Work (Qualifying) delivered on the University's Sydney or Fremantle (Perth) Campuses; Be eligible to apply for a Higher Education Sector Visa (Subclass 500).

The Scholarship is awarded as a partial tuition fee waiver and does not cover costs such as living expenses, accommodation, transport, overseas student health cover or any other cost associated with study.

records.title: Research project scholarship
records.description: This scholarship supports you to complete a higher degree by research while focusing on a specific project.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you meet:; the entry requirements for the relevant program:; Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program; Master of Philosophy (MPhil) program; any specific requirements of the project.

records.title: Zero Net Emissions Agriculture CRC Scholarship (guidance for on-farm greenhouse gas accounting)
records.description: Australian agriculture faces growing pressure to quantify, report, and reduce its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Yet the methodological foundations for on-farm GHG accounting remain inconsistent across industry calculators, national inventory methods, and voluntary reporting frameworks. Key unresolved issues, including the treatment of carbon opportunity costs, the permanence of carbon sequestration, the risk of double counting, and the management of reversal risk, create ambiguity for farmers, agribusiness, and policymakers alike, and undermine confidence in emissions reduction claims. This PhD scholarship, funded through the Zero Net Emissions Agriculture CRC (ZNE-Ag CRC), will address these gaps by developing rigorous, nationally consistent guidance for on-farm GHG accounting in Australia. The candidate will focus on land use and carbon sequestration, analysing how methodological choices within accounting frameworks influence incentives for farmers and agribusiness, and how they affect the attribution of emissions reductions across supply chains. The research will be conducted in alignment with international best practice and will seek to harmonise approaches across industry tools, scheme and reporting requirements.
records.amount_comment: This scholarship supports a PhD candidate to develop nationally consistent, practical guidance for on-farm greenhouse gas accounting in Australian agriculture, as part of the Zero Net Emissions Agriculture CRC. The research will examine how the treatment of carbon opportunity costs, permanence, and double-counting risks shapes farmer and agribusiness incentives, and how emissions reductions and sequestration can be recognised in a rigorous, transparent, and equitable manner. Outcomes will inform industry calculators, inventory methods, and reporting frameworks, with guidance co-designed with industry for integration into farm management tools.

records.title: The Henry and Jean Speagle Scholarship
records.description: Henry Speagle joined the Tintern Community some 60 years ago when he was appointed to the School Council by the Archbishop-In-Council. He remained a member of the School Council for nearly 40 years; in the final years of his term he was the Deputy Chairman. Among many contributions, his skill as an historian was put to good use in supporting the production of the School’s centenary history in 1977. Jean stood by Henry’s side on many occasions, supporting and enjoying many formal and celebratory events and activities, particularly those with a musical flavour. In 2001 Henry was inducted as a Life Governor of the School and in further recognition, in 1991, the Science block of classrooms was named in his honour, recognising his enormous contribution to the strength and development of Tintern Grammar. In 2019 the Speagle family was honoured when the building was refurbished and renamed as the Speagle Science Centre. Now in her 95th year, Jean continues to enjoy her connection to the Tintern Community and even though unable to attend in person, keeps up to date with the happenings around the school.The Henry and Jean Speagle Scholarship has been pledged to the school by Henry and Jean and their son. Following Henry’s death in 2020, the Speagle family made an initial gift to the Scholarship Fund. The family will continue to build the corpus for the Scholarship (including through a bequest) until a 50% Scholarship can be awarded in perpetuity to suitable recipients.Applicants must meet all or most of the criteria to be considered for the scholarship.The conditions are:A female student who does not currently attend Tintern GrammarFrom a family who for financial reasons could not otherwise afford the benefit of a Tintern educationA family (or student) who has an affiliation and is a practising member of a recognised Christian denomination, preferably Anglican.The scholarship will be awarded on the basis of the student’s application as well as the results from an independent academic examination, school reports and NAPLAN results, along with an interview with a senior member of staff and meeting the above criteria. This scholarship is aimed at those who would not normally have the financial means to attend Tintern Grammar and is means tested. Shortlisted candidates will be required to provide financial disclosure upon request.

records.title: Summer Vacation Research Scholarship
records.description: Put your summer holidays to good use with a six-week Summer Vacation Research Scholarship. You’ll gain valuable research experience working with our renowned supervisors to participate in a research project. If you’re a talented undergraduate science student enrolled in your second year or above, it’s an opportunity worth applying for.
records.eligibility: You must be currently enrolled in second-year or above of an undergraduate program in the Faculty of Science or a science-related discipline at UNSW or another Australian university. You must be able to be engaged in a project on a full-time basis (35 hours/week for six weeks during normal working hours unless advised otherwise by the supervisor). Projects must focus on research-based activities (administration tasks are not regarded as research) and should be completed by the end of February. Each successful candidate can hold only ONE such scholarship at a time. Students who were previously awarded a UNSW Science Vacation Research Scholarship are not eligible to apply.
records.amount_comment: Each scholarship is $3800 for a six-week research project.

records.title: Alex Rodgers Travel Grant
records.description: Each year the Research School of Astronomy & Astrophysics (RSAA) may offer approximately two awards known as the Alex Rodgers Travel Grant (the Award). Funding for this Award has been made possible due to an endowment from Mrs Ruth Rodgers in memory of her late husband Professor Alexander Rodgers. Professor Rodgers was a distinguished academic in the field of stellar astronomy and globular clusters, serving as School Director from 1987 to 1992. Professor Rodgers most significant contribution to the field was his involvement in the MACHO project, an international search for dark matter. The objective of the Award is to assist a student currently enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy in Astronomy & Astrophysics to travel abroad to attend scientific meetings and/or to work with astronomers at another institution on some chosen research project of direct relevance to the thesis work being undertaken.
records.eligibility: Full-time current RSAA PhD student. A successful applicant is ineligible to apply again. Australian and New Zealand citizens; Permanent residents of Australia; International students.

records.title: ANU-CSC Scholarship
records.description: The China Scholarship Council (CSC) is a non-profit institution affiliated with the People's Republic of China (PRC) Ministry of Education. CSC is responsible for the organization, management and provision of financial resources for Chinese citizens studying abroad, and to international students studying in China. CSC and ANU have established the China Scholarship Council - Australian National University Joint Funding Program to provide research opportunities to high quality research students and scholars from the PRC. Through this program, selected PRC students may be offered an ANU-CSC Postgraduate (PhD) Scholarship for a maximum of 48 months. Visiting scholars, postdoctoral fellows and PhD students from the PRC may also be provided funding to conduct research at ANU for a maximum of one or two years.
records.eligibility: Be a citizen and permanent resident of the PRC at the time of application; Meet all ANU admissions entry requirements including the English proficiency requirement, and receive either an unconditional offer of a place in an ANU PhD program, or an offer conditional on completion of their current program; Be selected by their ANU College or Research School for an HDR Fee Remission Merit Scholarship; Be eligible to receive an Australian student visa; Return to China at the end of the period of study; Satisfy other selection criteria set out by the China Scholarship Council.
records.amount_comment: Full tuition and stipend

records.description: Each year, the Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics (RSAA) in the ANU College of Science may offer an award known as the Bok Honours Year Scholarship in Astrophysics. The objective of the award is to support students with an outstanding academic record to undertake their Honours year in Astronomy and Astrophysics with the Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics in the ANU College of Science. The Scholarship is offered in honour of the late Professor Bart J. Bok, a former Director of the Mount Stromlo and Siding Spring Observatories from 1957 to 1966 and Professor of Astronomy at the Australian National University.
records.eligibility: is a domestic or international student; is enrolled/enrolling in the Astronomy and Astrophysics Honours Year within the Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics in the ANU College of Science.

records.title: Clark Davis Ivins Memorial Travel Grant
records.description: The Clark Davis Ivins Memorial Endowment in 2014 by the family of Private Clark Davis Ivins, an Australian soldier who died during World War II. He was just 24-years-old when he died of wounds received at the Battle of Milne Bay in Papua New Guinea in 1942. His life may have been a short one, but the part he played in the Battle of Milne Bay, a battle that was the first Japanese defeat on land in the Pacific War, is one that certainly made a difference to the lives of many Australians, both young and old, today. To commemorate the 75th Anniversary of the Battle of Milne Bay in 2017, the Endowment was expanded to offer the Clark Davis Ivins Memorial Travel Grant.
records.eligibility: a domestic or international student; enrolled in a Bachelor of International Security Studies; participating in a Global Learning Program offered by the ANU

records.title: Jason Passioura Bursary

This Bursary recognises Jasons outstanding contribution to research, in particular Jasons achievements in using spatial analysis to inform suicide prevention research; work carried out at the NCEPH as a collaboration between GRAPHC (the National Centre for Geographic Resources & Analysis in Primary Health Care) and the Black Dog Institute. Funding for this Award has been provided by NCEPH. The Jason Passioura Bursary will continue Jasons legacy, by each year funding one or more students or researchers (academic Level A or B or professional staff) to undertake activity in pursuit of their research goals. The Bursary is intended to support the use of high-quality data in research. Given Jasons commitment to spatial analyses especially regarding suicide prevention, applications that relate to these areas will be considered favourably.

records.title: Tom and Dorothy Cook Scholarships in Public Health and Tropical Medicine
records.description: The original Cook family migrated from England to Australia in 1837. 75 years later Tom's father purchased land in Mackay and in 1915 built a family home, which is currently known as Greenmount Homestead. In 1950 Tom Cook wed Dorothy Drysdale, a successful businesswoman, owning and running a ladies' fashion and beauty shop in Brisbane. Tom and Dorothy settled at the Mackay residence, where they lived for most of their 31-year marriage. The passing of Tom and Dorothy in 1981 and 1995 respectively ended eighty years of the Cook family residing at Greenmount. In 1984, Dorothy gifted the homestead to the Mackay Regional Council. Dorothy left a final gift to the community of Mackay in the form of a research scholarship at James Cook University. These scholarships are offered to higher degree research students to undertake a Master of Philosophy or Doctor of Philosophy in the field of public health, laboratory and clinical investigation of population health in Tropical Northern Australia.
records.eligibility: The Tom and Dorothy Cook scholarships in Public Health and Tropical Medicine will be open to competition among candidates who:; Are commencing, or in the process of applying for, a Master of Philosophy (MPhil) or Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) at JCU; Have a primary or secondary supervisor based in JCU’s Discipline of Public Health; Have a research project related to public health, laboratory and clinical investigations of population health; An significant element of the research project focusses on the Mackay and central Queensland region and; Meet JCU's admission requirements for MPhil or PhD degree.

records.description: We are looking to recruit up to three PhD students through the recently awarded Industry Fellowship for the Integrative geophysics Under cover: getting images of the Unknown Unknown project, supported by the Australia Research Council, the University of Western Australia (UWA), the Geological Survey of Western Australia (GSWA), and the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO). The goal of the project is to develop and extend new algorithms for integrating geophysical and geological data in undercover exploration scenarios at different scales, with applications to idealised and real-world data from Western Australia provided by GSWA. The methods to be investigated include geometrical (geophysical) inversion, trans-dimensional inversion, multi-physics integration, the integration of geophysical inversion with geological modelling.
