At La Trobe, our students gain essential skills in programming, data analysis, and machine learning, equipping them to shape the future of technology. As AI continues to evolve, so will the strong demand for artificial intelligence professionals in the public and private sectors, including opportunities in digital healthcare, smart manufacturing, smart cities, sustainable energy infrastructure, precision agriculture and more.
records.eligibility: To be eligible to apply for this scholarship, applicants must:; Be a new, international student commencing their course on the intake mentioned on their offer letter.; Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country other than Australia or New Zealand; Not be a humanitarian or other permanent visa holder.; Be a full fee-paying student (non-sponsored); Be eligible for direct entry to the programs.; Meet all course academic and English entry requirements and commence their studies at any of the LTU Victorian and Sydney campuses in 2026 or 2027.; Eligible students will have the scholarship applied to their offer letter, no application required.; All students must have passed the Genuine Student assessment, including financial checks, before they can be considered for this scholarship.; The scholarship may not be deferred to future intakes/years. If the recipient is unable to secure a student visa for that intake, the scholarship offer may be revoked.; Recipients are required to maintain full-time enrolment for the campus in their offer letter and demonstrate satisfactory academic progress throughout their studies.; Please refer to the Offer Letter for full terms and conditions.; Recipients will be required to participate in the International Scholarship Program events during their studies in Australia.; This scholarship can be combined with the Early Acceptance Grant to form a discount on first-year tuition fees. This is subject to all conditions being met for both offers.

records.title: Macquarie University Alumni Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to all eligible Macquarie University alumni international students for postgraduate studies.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship, you must be a full-time international student studying a Master level degree on-campus and meet the following criteria:; Be a graduate of a Macquarie University degree.; Meet the English and academic requirements for entry to your selected course.; Be accepted into a Macquarie University Postgraduate Coursework Degree (excludes offers for Master of Chiropractic, Clinical Neuropsychology, Organisational Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Clinical Audiology, or Speech and Language Pathology; a Non Award course; or a Doctor of Medicine or Physiotherapy).
records.amount_comment: 10% of total tuition fees

records.title: Women in Engineering Scholarship
records.description: At Monash, we support bright young women who wish to study engineering. If you are a high-achieving student intending to pursue an undergraduate degree at Monash in engineering, you may be eligible for this scholarship. No application is required. You will be automatically assessed when you list Monash as a VTAC preference.
records.eligibility: A female student currently in Year 12 or IB.; Must achieve minimum ATAR of 90.00; Commencing any engineering undergraduate single or double degree included in the degrees offered by the Monash Faculty of Engineering in Australia.

records.title: Monash University-Vietnam Government PhD Scholarship
records.description: This joint scholarship program supports high-achieving Vietnamese candidates to undertake a PhD at Monash University. Applicants can elect to study at a Monash campus in Australia or be based at a Vietnamese University, jointly supervised as an external offshore candidate. The program aims to address Vietnam's future industry and workforce needs, prioritising key research areas such as digital technologies, physics, biotechnologies and energy & environment.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; a citizen or permanent resident of Vietnam at the time of your application; meet Monash's competitive scholarship selection process requirements; meet Monash English language proficiency requirements.
records.amount_comment: Varies - see benefits

records.title: Nutrition Science Scholars Scholarship
records.description: The Nutrition Science Scholars Scholarship has been introduced to recognise the excellence of our students who will be enrolled in the Bachelor of Nutrition Science (Scholar Program).As a Scholar Scholarship student, you’ll be guaranteed entry into our Master of Nutrition and Dietetics (provided you maintain a 70+ WAM through your nutrition studies)
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; A commencing student intending to enrol in the Bachelor of Nutrition Science-Scholars Program (M2001) single degree in the Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences at a Monash campus in Australia.; ATAR 90+ or ATAR 70+ for Indigenous Australians; A current Year 12 or IB student, or completed Year 12 or IB in the year immediately prior to course commencement and has not undertaken any other tertiary study, and are applying for a new course through VTAC.
records.amount_comment: $3000 per 48 credit points of study for the minimum number of credit points required to complete the degree to a maximum of three years

records.title: DEPM Prostate Cancer Research Scholarship
records.description: The DEPM Prostate Cancer Research Scholarship is intended to encourage students to undertake further studies at Honours level in medicine at the Monash Alfred campus in the area of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, focusing principally on improving health outcomes for men diagnosed with prostate cancer.
records.eligibility: Australian or New Zealand citizen, holder of an Australian permanent resident visa, permanent humanitarian visa or international student.; Obtain a minimum weighted average mark (WAM) of 70% or above, across undergraduate study in Bachelor of Medical Sciences (Honours) (MED4301 & MED4302), Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences (Honours) (BMS4100 & BMS4200), or the Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours) (HSC4011, HSC4001 & 4002).; Commencing or continuing in a full-time School of Public Health and Preventive Medicine Honours program at the Monash Alfred campus (Bachelor of Medical Sciences (Honours) (MED4301 & MED4302), Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences (Honours) (BMS4100 & BMS4200), or the Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours) (HSC4011, HSC4001 & 4002)).
records.amount_comment: $3000 for one year only.

records.title: Verrocchi Charity Fund Pharmacy Prato Scholarship
records.description: The scholarship provides support to students in the Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences undertaking an international immersion through the Monash Global Campus Intensive program in Prato. This program builds the cultural competence and global perspectives needed to deliver inclusive healthcare.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Current student enrolled in one of the following courses at a Monash campus in Australia:; P3001 Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours); P6001 Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) and Master of Pharmacy; Approved to participate in Monash Global Campus Intensives (MGCI) in Italy for PHR5052 and are:; Domestic student experiencing financial hardship or are Indigenous Australian; Domestic or International student with minimum Weighted Average Mark of 80%. (Preference will be given to students in the Dean’s Scholars Program).

records.title: Ross Booth Honours Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded in memory of Ross Booth (1952-2024), a long-serving member of the Department of Economics and Course Director of the BCom and BEc at the Clayton and Malaysia campuses. An enthusiastic supporter of the BCom Honours program, and educational opportunity in general, Dr Booth supervised a large number of honours students with rigour, warmth and empathy. At the time of his sudden passing, Dr Booth was supervising an honours student and two PhD students. Dr Booth was a mentor and friend to countless colleagues and students at Monash University, and in the broader sports economics, sports history, and sports community.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing student enrolled in the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) or Bachelor of Economics (Honours) in the Monash Business School at the Monash Clayton campus.; ATAR 98+ or ATAR 85+ for Indigenous Australians (Students applying through VTAC)

records.title: Medicine and Artificial Intelligence Honours Scholarship
records.description: The Monash Interdisciplinary Research Academy of Medical AI (MIRAMA) is a collaborative Honours initiative that brings together expertise from the Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences (FMNHS), the Faculty of Information Technology (FIT), and the Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences (FPPS). Designed for high-achieving students, MIRAMA provides a unique opportunity to undertake interdisciplinary research at the intersection of health, medicine, and artificial intelligence. Through this initiative, Honours students will engage in innovative research projects that combine biomedical science, clinical and health research, artificial intelligence, data science, and digital technologies to address some of the most pressing challenges in healthcare. Projects may explore areas such as disease mechanisms, diagnostics, therapeutics, precision medicine, healthcare delivery, and emerging digital health solutions.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Commencing student enrolled in one of the following programs and undertaking a project from the MIRAMA program:; Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences (FMNHS); Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours); Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Honours); Bachelor of Medical Science (Honours) (BMedSci (Hons)); Faculty of Information Technology (FIT); Bachelor of Computer Science (Honours); Bachelor of Computer Science (Advanced); Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences (FPPS); Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours); WAM 70+
records.amount_comment: $6000 per 48 credit points of study for one year honours only.

records.title: Wilson Transformer Company Engineering Leadership Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to a high-achieving student who is currently enrolled in third year of an electrical and computer systems engineering degree in the Faculty of Engineering.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; Currently enrolled in an engineering degree in the Faculty of Engineering at a Monash campus in Australia

records.title: Department of Economics Honours Merit Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to high achieving students who enter into the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) or the Bachelor of Economics (Honours) course.
records.eligibility: You must meet the following criteria:; A commencing student, enrolling full-time in economics or jointly in economics and econometrics in the Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) degree or Bachelor of Economics (Honours) degree at the Monash Clayton campus.

records.title: International Talent Scholarship
records.description: A new scholarship for 2026 that covers tuition fees, with eligibility based on your prior academic achievements.
records.eligibility: You must:; meet the academic entry requirements; have an eligible nationality; meet minimum English language entry requirements for the course; be commencing the course for the first time; receive an admission offer letter into one of the eligible courses.
records.amount_comment: You'll receive an ongoing scholarship to cover 20% of your tuition fees per semester of study at QUT

records.title: China Scholarship Council Scholarship
records.description: A scholarship for future research students studying in any faculty.
records.eligibility: You must:; meet the China Scholarship Council requirements, as outlined on the China Scholarship Council website (in Mandarin); apply for and be admitted to a PhD, research masters or professional doctorate at QUT; To apply for this scholarship, you must meet the entry requirements for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master of Philosophy, or professional doctorate at QUT, including any English language requirements for international students. You must:; meet the China Scholarship Council requirements, as outlined on the China Scholarship Council website (in Mandarin); apply for and be admitted to a PhD, research masters or professional doctorate at QUT; To apply for this scholarship, you must meet the entry requirements for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master of Philosophy, or professional doctorate at QUT, including any English language requirements for international students.
records.amount_comment: a tuition fee waiver for the duration of your course, which is normally 1.5 years for masters students and 3 years for doctoral students.

records.title: COBL Academic Merit Scholarships for Vietnam
records.description: This scholarship provides financial assistance to outstanding students from Vietnam.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of Vietnam and be applying offshore from Vietnam (RMIT Vietnam students who completed cross-campus studies and immediately apply for the same qualification (program) in Melbourne campus are not eligible); be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; achieve Australian equivalent grade GPA of 3.0 or 75% average in your qualifying qualification at the time of application; hold a full or conditional offer letter to commence studies in Bachelor’s degree, Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma or Masters by Coursework programs offered by: School of Accounting, Information Systems and Supply Chain, School of Economics, Finance and Marketing, School of Management; not be an existing RMIT University student (existing ELICOS or Foundation Studies may be qualified and will be notified after Foundation Studies completion).
records.amount_comment: 25% tuition fee reduction for the eligible program(s) duration outlined on your offer letter.

records.title: College of Design and Social Context Student Bursary
records.description: This bursary provides financial assistance to international students studying in the College of Design and Social Context (DSC).
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the commencement of your degree; have existing offer letter (full or conditional offer) and be a commencing student in:; Semester 2 2026 intake in any College of Design and Social Context course (excluding Master by Research or PhD); Semester 3 2026 intake for Master of Project Management, Master of Energy Efficient and Sustainable Building; achieve Australian equivalent grade GPA of 2.0 or 60% average or ATAR 60 in your qualifying qualification at the time of application; not be an existing RMIT student (including RMIT Vietnam students); not be receiving another RMIT-funded scholarship or external sponsorship covering tuition fees
records.amount_comment: The total value of the bursary is a AU$5,000, one-off payment towards future tuition fees to be paid after the first census date into student's university account.

records.title: Medibank High Achiever International Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship, valued at AU$20,000, is available to international students studying Australian Year 12 or International Baccalaureate in Australia.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship, you must:; be applying from Australia; be a current year 12 student in Australia graduating in 2026; be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; submit your application via VTAC and receive an offer from RMIT for an Associate degree or Undergraduate degree; not be an existing RMIT student.
records.amount_comment: The total value of the scholarship is AU$20,000, to be paid to recipient's Australian bank account in AU$10,000 installments after the census date of each semester of the first year.

records.title: Pathway Scholarship for China
records.description: This scholarship supports students from China to study a Bachelor program at RMIT University in Melbourne, Australia.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR); be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; hold a Bachelor* offer commencing in 2026 or later that is packaged with ELICOS, Foundation Studies or Fast Track University Pathway, a Vocational Education (VE), or Associate Degree program. Students who have a packaged offer and are currently enrolled or recently completed a pathway program(s) will be eligible.; not be an existing RMIT University student studying a Bachelor program
records.amount_comment: The value of the scholarship is a 20% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the eligible Bachelor program(s) as outlined in your offer letter.

records.title: RMIT Vietnam Alumni Postgraduate Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship is awarded to RMIT Vietnam alumni who will commence Master by Coursework program at RMIT Australia.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be alumni who completed a degree at an RMIT Vietnam campus. This can include:; an undergraduate degree or postgraduate degree (including those who undertake exchange for up to 1 year in RMIT Melbourne campuses); packaged RMIT Vietnam Undergraduate and RMIT Melbourne Postgraduate offer holders; have an offer letter and enrol in one of Masters by Coursework program at RMIT Australia.
records.amount_comment: 10% tuition fee reduction for the program duration outlined on your offer letter.

records.title: School of Education Academic Merit Scholarship for China
records.description: This scholarship supports outstanding students from China to pursue their academic goals in education or teaching discipline at RMIT University in Melbourne, Australia.
records.eligibility: In order to qualify for this scholarship you must:; be a citizen of the People’s Republic of China (including Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR); be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement; achieve Australian equivalent grade GPA of 2.5 or 70% average or ATAR 75 in your qualifying qualification at the time of application; hold a full or conditional offer letter in one of the eligible programs: Bachelor of Education, Master of Teaching Practice (Primary Education), Master of Teaching Practice (Secondary Education); not be an existing RMIT University student studying one of the eligible programs.
records.amount_comment: The value of the scholarship is a 20% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the eligible program(s) as outlined in your offer letter.

records.title: Preparing for Success Pathway Scholarship
records.description: The Preparing for Success Pathway Scholarship which will assist students transition into their chosen degree. The scholarship supports students through an initial preparatory program (Preparing for Success Program) where the student gains skills required for successful degree studies. Upon successful completion of Preparing for Success Program students will be able to progress onto a bachelor program. A bonus payment will be made upon commencement of study in the student's chosen Bachelor degree.
records.eligibility: Recipients must be:; Commencing Preparing for Success pathway program in 2027; Be offered the Preparing for Success program as an Early Offer; Complete Preparing for Success in 2027; Progress immediately into the first available offering of the packaged Bachelor degree upon completion of the Preparing for Success program

records.title: Bangladesh $10,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship offers talented international students from Bangladesh AUD $10,000 per year towards their studies at Macquarie University. The scholarship is available for the full duration of an eligible Bachelor's and Master's coursework degree. For students enrolled in sessions, AUD $10,000 will be credited in the second session of the first year of enrolment, followed by AUD $5,000 credited in each subsequent session for the remainder of the degree. For students enrolled in tems, AUD $7,500 will be credited in the third term of the first year of enrolment, followed by AUD $2,500 credited in each subsequent term for the remainder of the degree.
records.eligibility: Be an international full fee-paying student. Be a citizen of Bangladesh. Be commencing full-time in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Macquarie University in 2027 and beyond (excluding Graduate Certificates, Bachelor of Clinical Science, Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours), Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Physiotherapy, Master of Clinical Audiology, Master of Clinical Psychology, Master of Clinical Neuropsychology, Master of Organisational Psychology, Master of Professional Psychology, Master of Speech and Language Pathology). Accept your Letter of Offer and pay the commencement fee by the Acceptance Deadline. Must not be a recipient of a government sponsorship or scholarship that covers full tuition fees, unless approved by Macquarie University Scholarships Team. Please note: The annual number of scholarship recipients may vary according to the availability of funding and the number of eligible candidates and will only be confirmed when an offer letter is made.
records.amount_comment: Applicants will be assessed automatically for this scholarship. Successful candidates will receive the scholarship with their Course Letter of Offer.

records.title: Macquarie Advantage Humanitarian Scholarship
records.description: The Macquarie Advantage Humanitarian Scholarship provides full tuition fee support for students from refugee and asylum‑seeking backgrounds to undertake undergraduate study at Macquarie University.This scholarship is awarded for the full duration of the course, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility criteria.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for this scholarship, applicants must meet the following criteria:Be from a refugee or asylum-seeking background, including those with lived experience of displacement.Hold a Temporary Protection Visa (subclass V785), or Safe Haven Enterprise Visa (SHEV) (subclass V790), or Bridging Visa (BV) A (subclass V010)*, or Bridging Visa (BV) E (Subclass V050 or V051)*, or Temporary Humanitarian Stay (subclass V786), or Temporary Humanitarian Stay (subclass V449).*Applicants holding a bridging visa will also need to submit a letter or relevant documentation from a recognised organisation supporting their status as a refugee or asylum seeker and must ensure they have Australian study rights whilst holding that visa.Receive an offer of admission to an undergraduate degree at Macquarie University and intend to commence study in the year the scholarship is offered.Demonstrate financial need.
records.amount_comment: 100% of total tuition fees

records.title: Pio and Marisa Iovenitti Memorial Engineering Excellence Scholarship 2027
records.description: The Pio and Marisa Iovenitti Memorial Scholarship honours Associate Professor Pio Iovenitti's contribution to Swinburne for over 30 years and his wife Marisa’s support. Pio was a respected leader, mentor and scholar within the School of Engineering, admired for his dedication and humility. This scholarship supports a postgraduate student in their final year of a Master of Engineering Science degree in any specialisation, continuing Pio’s legacy of excellence and commitment to education.
records.eligibility: Applicants must be:; an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or international resident.

records.title: Swinburne University Postgraduate Research Award
records.description: SUPRAs are awarded to students of exceptional research potential undertaking doctoral studies. The awards are provided to assist with general living costs. Tuition fees are also covered by the award. SUPRA scholarships are available to both future and current students enrolled in or applying for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Professional Doctorate course at Swinburne.
records.eligibility: meet the entry requirements for a PhD or Professional Doctorate as set out for their proposed program at Swinburne; hold a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours (or equivalent); propose a research project that aligns with a Swinburne Research Strategy and Ecosystem area; would not be receiving another stipend scholarship to support their general living costs while undertaking their course of study if that stipend is greater than 75 per cent of that student’s RTP Stipend or SUPRA scholarship stipend rate.

records.title: Alan and Helen Ross Forestry Education Scholarship
records.description: The Fenner School of Environment & Society may offer an award known as the Alan and Helen Ross Forestry Education Scholarship. The objective of the Award is to support a Papua New Guinea (PNG) citizen with interests and experience in PNG forests and forestry to study a graduate coursework program in forests. Funding for this Award has been provided by the Alan and Helen Ross Forestry Education Scholarship Trust. The Trust honours the life and work of Alan and Helen Ross, longtime residents of PNG who were deeply committed to its future. Alan was a highly respected figure in forestry in PNG, mentoring many of his PNG colleagues.
records.eligibility: The Award is available to a commencing ANU student who:; is an international student visa holder with PNG citizenship; holds an undergraduate qualification in forestry or a related discipline; or, in exceptional cases, does not hold such a qualification but possesses equivalent extensive professional experience in forestry; receives an offer of admission to one of the following programs: Master of Forests; Graduate Diploma in Science; Graduate Certificate in Forests

records.title: ANU Project 89 PhD Scholarship
records.description: Project 89 is an initiative of the Vietnamese government which aims to build capacity and academic training for Vietnamese university lecturers and executives. Its implementation is supported by the Australian government.
records.eligibility: Continuation based on academic performance

records.title: Digital Agriculture PhD Scholarship
records.description: ANU-CSIRO Digital Agriculture PhD Scholarship provides funding to support outstanding candidates to pursue a PhD program at ANU, where the focus of their research is on a collaborative project between CSIRO and ANU in the field of information science relevant to agriculture. Funding for this award has been provided by CSIRO’s Data61 - Australia' leading data innovation group. Their mission is to create Australia’s data driven future by building the world’s leading data-focused research and innovation powerhouse.
records.eligibility: The Award will be available to a prospective domestic or international candidate who:; is enrolled or enrolling full-time in a program of study for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in the field of Information Science relevant to the Agriculture domain, based in the either the ANU College of Science and Medicine or the ANU College of Systems and Society; will be undertaking research for CSIRO / ANU projects under a Collaboration Agreement; has demonstrated First class honours (H1), or equivalence; have signed a Student Agreement with CSIRO, unless otherwise agreed in writing with CSIRO; must not be in full-time employment.
records.amount_comment: $39,069 per annum and $15,000 per annum supplementary scholarship

records.title: William Bardsley Award
records.description: The William Bardsley Award is offered to students who are enrolled in the Bachelor of Music or Master of Music specialising in violin performance and are experiencing financial need.
records.eligibility: To be considered, you must be enrolled in either the Bachelor of Music or Master of Music (or their successors) specialising in violin performance.

records.title: Grace Ella Fraser Fund
records.description: The Grace Ella Fraser Fund is offered to undergraduate cello students at the Melbourne Conservatorium of Music who have outstanding talent and are in financial need.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must be enrolled in the Bachelor of Music specialising in Cello.

records.title: Harry Hains Memorial Theatre Bursaries
records.description: The Harry Hains Memorial Theatre Bursaries were established with a gift from the Helen and David Hains Foundation and are awarded to students who are enrolled with the Victorian College of the Arts in a degree in a field of theatre and are experiencing financial disadvantage.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this bursary, you must be enrolled in one of the Bachelor of Fine Arts (Theatre), Bachelor of Fine Arts (Acting), Bachelor of Fine Arts Honours (Theatre), Bachelor of Fine Arts Honours (Acting), Master of Theatre (Dramaturgy), Master of Theatre (Directing) or Master of Theatre (Writing) in the year for which the bursary is awarded.

records.title: GAM Scott Research Award
records.description: The GAM Scott Research Award was established with a gift from friends and associates of George Anderson MacDonald Scott and is offered to students or graduate researchers enrolled in a research degree in Botany in the areas of bryophytes or plant ecology who are undertaking field work. Preference will be given to research work involving bryophytes.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this award, you must:; Be enrolled in Honours or PhD in the field of Botany in the School of Bioscience; Be undertaking research that involves field work the area of bryophytes or plant ecology.

records.title: Califole Melbourne Medical School Scholarship
records.description: The Califole Melbourne Medical School Scholarship is offer to students who are enrolled in the Doctor of Medicine, have completed their secondary schooling in a state or territory government school, and are experiencing financial disadvantage. Preference is given to students who are from a regional or remote area of Australia.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Be enrolled in the first year of the Doctor of Medicine; Have completed secondary schooling in a state or territory government school.

records.title: Cbus Super Mavis Robertson Scholarship
records.description: The Cbus Super Mavis Robertson Scholarship is offered to Bachelor of Commerce students who are experiencing disadvantaged circumstances. Preference is given to female students.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Be completing at least 100 points of the Bachelor of Commerce (at the time of application); Be enrolling in the second year of the Bachelor of Commerce

records.title: Gretna Weste Plant Pathology & Mycology Scholarship
records.description: The Gretna Weste Plant Pathology & Mycology Scholarship is awarded to talented students who are engaged in honours or graduate research in the field of plant pathology or mycology in the University of Melbourne School of BioSciences.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must be enrolled in honours or graduate research in the field of plant pathology or mycology, in the School of BioSciences.

records.title: Suzanne and Geoffrey Dawson Scholarship
records.description: The scholarship is awarded to a high-achieving student enrolled in the Professional Learning Capstone as part of a Master of Teaching, and pursuing research in the field of education, the outcome of which is likely to enhance the advancement of social justice in educational settings and provide equality of access to improved facilitation of learning, in identified communities.
records.eligibility: To be considered for this scholarship, you must:; Be enrolled in a Professional Learning Capstone subject as part of a Master of Teaching program; Be pursuing research in the field of education through the Professional Learning Capstone, the outcome of which is likely to enhance the advancement of social justice in educational settings and provide equality of access to improved facilitation of learning, in identified communities.

records.title: Florence Davey Pianoforte Scholarship
records.description: This Scholarship was first established in 1983 and was funded by donations in excess of $50,000 from Miss Florence M. Davey. The Scholarship fund continues to be maintained by UQ on trust. Miss Florence M. Davey, Associate, Licentiate and Fellow of Trinity College of Music, London, taught music until the age of 90 and was dedicated to the pursuit of excellence in piano performance.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you:; will be enrolled full-time in the first year of the Bachelor of Music or a dual program that includes the Bachelor of Music.

records.title: Project 89-UQ Scholarship
records.description: Project 89 is a Vietnamese Government initiative that builds capacity and academic expertise among Vietnamese university lecturers and senior leaders. The Australian Government supports the delivery of this initiative.
records.eligibility: You will be eligible for this scholarship if you:; are a citizen of Vietnam; satisfy the selection criteria set by Vietnam government scholarship (Project 89); satisfy UQ's admissions entry requirement and be offered a place in the PhD program; meet the University's English proficiency requirement.
records.amount_comment: Living allowance, health insurance in Australia, one return airfare from Vietnam to Australia, and tuition fees

records.title: UQ Refugee and Humanitarian Scholarship
records.description: The UQ Refugee and Humanitarian Scholarship is funded by The University of Queensland (UQ). Established in 2021, this Scholarship offers students from refugee or asylum seeker backgrounds the opportunity to pursue higher education in any desired discipline at UQ.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you:; are or will be enrolled in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program at UQ; hold one of the following Australian visas:; Temporary Protection Visa (subclass 785), Safe Haven Enterprise Visa (subclass 790), Temporary Humanitarian Concern Visa (subclass 786), Temporary Humanitarian Stay Visa (subclass 449); any other similar visa from time to time that the Australian government might enact for people from refugee or asylum seeker backgrounds; Bridging Visa E (subclass 050) or Bridging Visa A (subclass 010) if you have applied for any of the above-mentioned visas.; have not received the Scholarship previously for the same level of study; do not hold another similar scholarship; can demonstrate financial hardship by providing documentary evidence.
records.amount_comment: 100% tuition fee waiver, plus $29,000 annual living stipend

records.title: UQ LGBTQIA+ Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship was established in 2013 and maintained by gifts from donors including UQ staff, alumni and friends.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you:; identify as a member of the LGBTQIA+ community; are or will be enrolled in an Approved Program in the semester of the award; can demonstrate financial hardship by providing documentary evidence; can demonstrate commitment to the LGBTQIA+ community; have not previously received the scholarship.

records.title: Calboonya Legacy Information Technology and Computer Science Scholarship
records.description: Established in 2019 this scholarship is maintained by a gift from a UQ Bachelor of Computer Science (1979) alumni husband and wife, who in recognition of the encouragement they received to pursue their education would like to leave a legacy for students who may not otherwise have the opportunity to study in the areas of computer science and information technology at UQ.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you:; are a commencing student or a prior recipient of this scholarship; can demonstrate financial need; do not hold a scholarship that the Associate Dean considers to be similar.

records.title: The Kym Broadhurst Bursary for the Visually Impaired
records.description: This scholarship was established in 2000 and is maintained by gifts from the family of Kym Broadhurst, to encourage excellence in undergraduate or postgraduate study for visually impaired students.
records.eligibility: You're eligible if you:; are visually impaired (corrected vision must be less than 6:60); enrolled in an undergraduate or postgraduate program
records.amount_comment: Currently held in tenure until 2028.

records.title: Larsen Jewellery Design Scholarship Program
records.description: Awarded to a design student with an interest and passion for jewelley, design or visual art.
records.eligibility: Please Contact University of Canberra for more information about Eligibility
